shared: The Behemoth II Heavy Tank represents Aldis Industries' answer to the original Behemoth's most persistent tactical liability. Where the standard design sacrificed speed entirely for firepower and armor, the Behemoth II installs a Vlar 300 XL fusion engine that more than doubles the vehicle's ground speed while preserving its formidable armament and advanced ferro-fibrous protection. Developed in the late Republic era, the Behemoth II earned a reputation early in its service life as the best tank no one wanted, as commanders balked at its price point and the logistical demands of its XL powerplant. That skepticism largely evaporated following a series of high-profile engagements during the Capellan Crusades, where Behemoth IIs demonstrated an almost legendary resistance to destruction even under sustained BattleMech assault.

The Behemoth II's primary armament is a single Poland Main Model C Gauss rifle providing precise long-range firepower comparable to purpose-built tank destroyers. Eight Sian/Ceres Serval Thunderbolt 5 missile launchers complement this with independently controlled fire arcs: each gunnery station can be reconfigured on the fly to address different target sets, tracks up to ten contacts simultaneously, and maintains threat assessment for two per station. The four Death Blossom 10-Pack rocket launcher banks handle close-range engagements.

The Vlar 300 XL fusion engine pushes the Behemoth II to over 54 kph at maximum speed, a dramatic improvement over the original design that allows the vehicle to contest ground previously conceded to faster opponents. ArcShield Max III Advanced Ferro-Fibrous armor provides protection that has proven resilient even under sustained BattleMech-scale fire in documented engagements. The Omicron VIII targeting system delivers a seventeen percent improvement in acquisition speed and calculates long-range fire solutions thirty-one percent faster than comparable competitor systems, giving crews a meaningful edge at extended engagement ranges.

The XL engine that grants the Behemoth II its speed advantage is also its most significant vulnerability. Side-torso penetration that would be survivable in a standard design risks catastrophic engine failure in the Behemoth II, and this susceptibility to massed flank fire has influenced how commanders choose to deploy the vehicle.

Aldis Industries introduced the Behemoth II in the early Republic era as a premium successor to their long-running Behemoth production line, drawing on XL engine technology that had become available to Inner Sphere manufacturers following the end of the Jihad. The vehicle was expensive, the XL powerplant was logistically demanding, and many armored formation commanders preferred the proven simplicity of the standard Behemoth. To accelerate adoption, Aldis gifted the tank to numerous major commands between 3108 and 3110, and in the second half of 3110, sales doubled the number of units already in service through gifted examples.

The tank's reputation was settled during the Capellan Crusades. When elements of the Fourth Oriente Hussars raided Shuen Wan in 3117, a platoon of Behemoth IIs deployed by House Tsang Xiao and Kraken Unleashed held hull-down positions on a high desert plateau against a flanking assault by a medium BattleMech company led by Captain Jocelyn Teague in her Shockwave. Teague expected the tanks to withdraw once their defilade advantage was neutralized, but the Behemoth IIs held their ground under concentrated fire, dropping two 'Mechs at 500 meters before the attackers closed. By the time the surviving 'Mechs reached close range, the Behemoth IIs had reduced the attacking force by half, and all four tanks remained operational when the Hussars withdrew. The engagement was widely analyzed in armored warfare circles and contributed significantly to the Behemoth II's growing reputation for near-indestructibility in prepared defensive positions.

Production at Betelgeuse was disrupted during the Dark Age by XL engine shortages, forcing Aldis to temporarily resume output of the standard Behemoth chassis in the form of the Liao variant. The Terra line continued production uninterrupted under Republic of the Sphere management, maintaining Behemoth II availability for that state's armored formations throughout the early Dark Age. When the Republic collapsed, control of the Terra facility became a contested issue that mirrored broader conflicts over the planet's industrial infrastructure.

The Bellona Hover Tank is a forty-five-ton cavalry vehicle developed by Clan Hell's Horses during the Jihad era as part of Khan James Cobb's campaign to reassert the Horses' presence among the Inner Sphere Clans. Named for the Roman goddess of war, the vehicle was designed as a rapid strike and flanking platform, built around the Hell's Horses cavalry tenet that speed is the finest armor a vehicle can carry. First produced at HH Complex Beta in the Clan Homeworlds, the Bellona arrived in the Inner Sphere in limited numbers during the Jihad and quickly earned a fierce reputation among Hell's Horses warriors and their Clan opponents. The design has since become a mainstay of Hell's Horses toumans across multiple eras, valued for the combination of high-speed mobility and consistent firepower it delivers to fast cavalry formations.

The Bellona's primary offensive weapon is a Type 9 Ultra Autocannon/10 mounted in an armored turret, giving the crew the ability to engage targets across a broad range band whether advancing or withdrawing. The turret mount is central to the vehicle's tactical design, allowing the autocannon's reach to be applied regardless of the Bellona's direction of travel, a critical attribute for a vehicle whose doctrine emphasizes continuous forward pressure. Four Series HL-II Light Machine Guns and two Type 14b Flamers round out the weapons suite, providing meaningful anti-infantry and anti-Elemental capability. The flamers proved particularly useful in close engagements where Elementals would otherwise overwhelm a lighter vehicle, and they have become a signature component of the Bellona's tactical identity in Hell's Horses formations.

Eight tons of Forging HTT05 armor protect the hull and motive system, representing the maximum the designers could mount while preserving the vehicle's speed. Coverage prioritizes the forward hull, reflecting the design's preference for head-on engagement, though the turret is not neglected. A Fusion Type 170 powerplant provides a cruising speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour and a flank speed exceeding one hundred fifty, making the Bellona one of the fastest armed vehicles deployed by Hell's Horses. Series XII ComSys communications and Build IX TTS targeting systems are standard equipment. The design's primary limitation is the Light Machine Guns, which are most effective against unarmored infantry and offer little penetrating power against the armored opposition Hell's Horses most commonly faces on Clan front lines.

The Bellona's development grew from Clan Hell's Horses' frustration at their exclusion from the Clan Invasion and the subsequent wars over the Inner Sphere. Under the direction of Khan James Cobb, the Horses began planning a renewed offensive, and their scientist caste recognized an opportunity to field a purpose-built cavalry vehicle that matched the Horses' traditional emphasis on vehicles and Elementals over BattleMechs. The original design specification called for a tracked hull, but the Hell's Horses lead test pilot, a longtime cavalry warrior whose solahma had shaped his view of combat, argued that speed was paramount, reportedly insisting that velocity is the best armor. His persistence led to the hull being redesigned as a hover chassis, and the resulting vehicle exceeded the initial performance targets.

Production began at HH Complex Beta on Tiber in the Clan Homeworlds around 3070, but getting the new vehicles to the frontline Clusters proved difficult. The long chain of JumpShips required to ferry tanks from the Homeworlds to the Inner Sphere constrained supply severely, and barely six Stars of Bellonas arrived in time for the initial fighting against Clan Wolf and Clan Ice Hellion. Those that did arrive performed well in the field, and Bellona crews developed a reputation for aggressive close-in tactics that exploited the hover chassis's superior speed. Star Commander Dylan and his crew accumulated more Trials of Grievance than any other warriors in their Cluster, many fought against fellow Hell's Horses who underestimated the vehicle, with the most notable occurring on Nyserta against a Star Captain in an Ice Ferret. After extended maneuvering failed to establish a decisive range advantage, the Star Captain was maneuvered into a canyon where the Bellona's close-range weaponry proved decisive.

With Hell's Horses' eventual relocation to the Inner Sphere following the Jihad, production shifted to Csesztreg Industriplex Beta, which began building Bellonas in 3076. The expanded production base finally allowed the vehicle to reach frontline Clusters in meaningful numbers, and it rapidly became the standard fast cavalry platform in Hell's Horses toumans. The XL variant entered production in the early Dark Age, replacing the original engine with a lighter extralight unit to free tonnage for additional systems while preserving the hover chassis's characteristic speed. Production at Csesztreg continued through the ilClan era, sustaining the Bellona's role as a principal cavalry vehicle across multiple generations of Hell's Horses warriors.

The Blizzard Hover Transport is a light infantry carrier designed and produced by Kressly WarWorks of Epsilon Eridani, entering service in 3054. Conceived to give small militias and independent commands the ability to deliver troops rapidly across contested terrain, the design reflects Kressly's practical philosophy: affordable, reliable, and easy to maintain. The vehicle was originally intended to counter Clan mobile tactics, relying on extreme speed rather than armor or firepower to survive on a modern battlefield. It found its greatest success not in the Clan Invasion campaigns its designers envisioned, but among the fractious factions of the Chaos March, where its low acquisition cost and exceptional speed made it the transport of choice for underfunded armies, local defense forces, and mercenary commands that needed to move infantry quickly without exhausting their operational budgets.

The core of the Blizzard's appeal is its Nissan 95 internal combustion engine, which drives the twenty-five-ton hover chassis to a flank speed of 151 kilometers per hour. This performance allows the vehicle to close with enemy positions under a barrage from its single turret-mounted LongFire V LRM-5, deploy its passengers, and withdraw before absorbing sustained fire. The LRM-5 is deliberately light armament for a front-line vehicle, but it serves its purpose well: once the infantry bays are cleared, the launcher enables the Blizzard to contribute indirect suppression fire from extended range, keeping the vehicle out of direct engagement while still supporting the troops it delivered. The BlazeFire Sight Lock targeting system and Angst Clear Channel 3 communications suite give crews adequate situational awareness for a light transport role.

The cargo bay holds six tons of capacity, accommodating two standard infantry platoons or a single heavy infantry platoon without reducing the vehicle's speed rating. The ICE powerplant keeps manufacturing costs and logistical complexity low, a deliberate trade-off that broadens the Blizzard's appeal to operators without sophisticated maintenance infrastructure. The primary weakness of the design is its protection: three tons of StarSlab/3 armor can absorb only a limited number of direct hits before the hull is compromised. This vulnerability forces crews to treat the Blizzard as a true transport rather than a fighting vehicle, staying at range and avoiding direct engagement with anything heavier than infantry. For commands that understand its limitations, the Blizzard performs its role effectively; those that push it into the line of fire tend to lose it quickly.

Kressly WarWorks developed the Blizzard in the early 3050s with the goal of providing Chaos March worlds and independent commands an affordable transport capable of operating against the fast-moving Clan threat. The vehicle debuted in 3054, predating the formal dissolution of Federated Commonwealth authority over the former Sarna March. When Operation Guerrero shattered that authority in 3057 and dozens of worlds found themselves without the support of a major power, demand for cheap military hardware surged. Kressly, already producing the Blizzard at its Epsilon Eridani plant, was ideally positioned to meet that demand, and the transport became a common sight in the militias that formed across contested systems throughout the new March.

The design's first significant test in sustained operations came during the Capellan reunification war against the St. Ives Compact beginning in 3060. Infantry-heavy Capellan formations mobilized every available vehicle, and the Blizzard's speed proved critical during rapid assault and evacuation operations across the Compact's contested worlds. Multiple Warrior Houses fielded the transport to shuttle infantry squads between engagements, though casualties mounted when vehicles were pushed further forward than their armor could sustain. The campaign also exposed the Blizzard to direct competition with the Maultier Hover APC, which emerged as a short-range alternative. Kressly responded by developing two variants to preserve its market position: a simple swap to short-range missiles for closer-range engagements, and a dedicated escort design that traded the infantry bay for heavier armament and electronic countermeasures.

During the Jihad, the Word of Blake absorbed Epsilon Eridani into its Protectorate in the early 3070s, and Kressly's production facilities operated under Blakist oversight for most of that decade. The Epsilon Eridani Protectorate Militia became the primary operator of the Black Blizzard escort variant during this period, fielding it to protect supply convoys and support Blakist infantry operations. Coalition forces from the Federated Suns front of Operation SCOUR liberated the planet in February 3078 after a sharp week-long campaign, and production resumed under Republic of the Sphere administration. The Blizzard remained active in Republic service through the Dark Age as a reserve transport, fielded by garrison forces and planetary militias that valued its low cost and mechanical simplicity. When the Republic's authority collapsed in the 3130s, surviving vehicles dispersed across the successor states. The Capellan Confederation, which had reasserted regional dominance in the area surrounding Epsilon Eridani, continued to operate the Blizzard in logistical support roles into the ilClan era.

The Bolla Stealth Tank in its Republic of the Sphere configuration is a sixty-ton wheeled OmniVehicle developed by the Republic Armed Forces in 3084 as a covert battle armor delivery platform. Derived from a Word of Blake design uncovered during the Jihad, the Bolla was substantially reworked to match RAF organizational standards while retaining the stealth characteristics that made the original concept operationally valuable. Manufactured by Maxwell-Pulaski Motors at a concealed facility on Terra, the RotS Bolla entered service exclusively with Republic special forces and has been kept under deliberate operational security, with few outside the RAF aware that the new configurations exist. The design represents the Republic’s commitment to preserving specialized covert capabilities inherited from the conflict that defined its founding.

The Republic Bolla retains the stealth armor and wheeled mobility of its Blakist predecessor, maintaining the core capability that defined the original design’s operational value. Factory standard equipment includes a single machine gun, a C³ slave linking the vehicle into supporting tactical networks, and a Guardian ECM suite sustaining the stealth armor system. The infantry transport bay was redesigned around the RAF’s standard four-trooper squad, reducing its size compared to the Blakist original and freeing four additional tons of pod space for mission-specific weapons loads. The VOX 280 XL fusion plant delivers a cruising speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour and a flank speed of eighty-six, providing useful strategic mobility on road networks while the stealth system manages tactical survivability during approach.

The OmniVehicle architecture gives the RotS Bolla substantial mission flexibility. Nearly twenty tons of pod space, with up to fifteen tons accessible through the turret, accommodates configurations tailored to specific infiltration or direct-action requirements. The Baltex K590 targeting system and GPT Multi-Track Enhanced communications package ensure reliable coordination between the vehicle, its embarked troops, and C³-networked supporting units. The stealth system and pod-space adaptability are the design’s primary strengths. Its principal limitation is the thin fixed armament when stripped of pod weapons, making the vehicle dependent on completing its mission before heavier enemy forces can bring it to a stand-up fight.

The Word of Blake developed the original Bolla during the Jihad as a covert infiltration vehicle, deploying it from Krupp Armaments Works on Terra to support operations requiring undetected battle armor insertion. Coalition forces encountered captured examples in service with multiple factions who had salvaged them from Blakist engagements, but the design remained poorly understood until coalition analysts accessed the Blakist research facility where the vehicle had been developed. The technical intelligence gathered there proved far more complete than anything recoverable from field salvage, giving Republic-aligned engineers a solid foundation for a successor design.

At Devlin Stone’s direction, Maxwell-Pulaski Motors, operating a Terra facility already associated with the vehicle through earlier captured-equipment support work, was tasked with developing the revised platform. Engineers reduced the infantry bay to accommodate the RAF’s four-trooper squad standard, converting the recovered weight into additional pod capacity, and replaced the C³i system with a conventional C³ slave that simplified logistics without sacrificing network capability. The revamped Bolla entered production in 3084 and was delivered exclusively to Republic special forces units under strict operational security. The Republic’s deliberate secrecy around the new configurations meant that factions holding original Blakist examples remained unaware of the RotS variant’s improved capabilities for many years.

Production continued through the Dark Ages into the ilClan era, reflecting the enduring value Republic and successor-state special forces placed on covert battle armor delivery. Despite the disruption of the Fortress Republic period and subsequent political realignments across the Inner Sphere, Maxwell-Pulaski Motors maintained production sufficient to support ongoing special operations requirements.

The Bolla Stealth Tank is a sixty-ton wheeled combat vehicle developed by the Word of Blake as a specialized covert insertion platform during the Jihad era. Designed around stealth armor and an integrated C³i command-and-control network, the Bolla was conceived to deliver battle armor assets into contested objectives without triggering the sensor responses that betray a conventional troop transport. The design remained largely unknown until coalition forces uncovering a Blakist research facility yielded technical specifications more detailed than anything recoverable from battlefield salvage alone. Four configurations were produced at Krupp Armaments Works on Terra: the Invictus, which served as the primary variant, alongside the Dominus, Infernus, and Comminus. Captured examples spread among coalition forces following the Jihad, and the design’s fundamental architecture later provided the foundation for the Republic of the Sphere’s own stealth transport program.

The Bolla’s defining capability is its stealth armor system, which substantially degrades enemy targeting effectiveness at medium and long range and allows the vehicle to advance across open terrain with a survivability impossible for conventional wheeled transports. The single fixed machine gun serves as a deliberately minimal armament reflecting the vehicle’s primary role as a delivery platform rather than a direct combatant. The real striking power lies in the battle armor squad carried in the infantry bay, sized in original Blakist production for a full six-trooper Level I in accordance with Word of Blake organizational doctrine. A C³i system integrates the crew and embarked infantry into a unified targeting network with any linked C³i units nearby, allowing coordinated strikes with a precision difficult for conventional forces to match.

The turret accommodates variant-specific weapon loads that allow the Bolla to adapt to different tactical roles. The chassis design provides pod space for configurations ranging from close assault to long-range precision engagement, giving unit commanders mission flexibility that fixed-load vehicles cannot offer. The wheeled drive and XL fusion plant deliver a road speed that makes the vehicle difficult to overtake in pursuit scenarios, while the stealth system remains the primary defensive capability against detection during approach. The XL plant is a vulnerability, as battle damage to the engine compartment risks catastrophic power loss, a trade-off the designers accepted to preserve payload capacity for the infantry bay and weapons systems.

The Word of Blake developed the Bolla during the opening years of the Jihad as part of their investment in specialized covert-operations equipment. Production was established at Krupp Armaments Works on Terra, giving the Blakists a secure facility well within their home territory. The vehicle served throughout the Jihad supporting Blakist special operations, inserting C³i-networked Level I squads ahead of main force advances and into command targets selected for seizure. The design’s stealth characteristics allowed it to operate in situations where an armored column would have immediately drawn defensive fire.

Coalition forces encountered the Bolla repeatedly during the campaigns converging on Terra and recovered examples through battlefield salvage. Analysts accessing a Blakist research facility during these operations obtained technical specifications significantly more complete than anything field recovery had produced, giving Republic-aligned engineers a detailed understanding of the vehicle’s architecture. Following the fall of Blake’s Protectorate, ownership of the Terra production facilities passed to the nascent Republic of the Sphere, though the Krupp Armaments Works line was not reactivated for further Bolla production under Republic authority. Captured units entered the inventories of the Lyran Commonwealth, Federated Suns, Draconis Combine, and former Free Worlds states through post-Jihad salvage operations, though each faction’s holdings are small and maintenance of the stealth system presents ongoing technical challenges. The Republic retained the largest consolidated collection of original Bolla configurations and used that familiarity as the basis for the subsequent RotS redesign program.

The Browning Mobile Headquarters was an alternative mobile command vehicle that served alongside the original Star League Defense Force Mobile HQ during the final centuries of the Star League era. Produced by Mitchell Vehicles on Terra, the Browning was designed as a lighter, more accessible command platform for regiment-level and smaller formations. Where the standard Mobile HQ provided theater-level coordination with its seven tons of communications equipment, the Browning carried a reduced but still capable four-ton suite better matched to the needs of combined-arms commanders in the field. Its smaller footprint and simpler construction made it a practical choice for officers who valued tactical flexibility over the comprehensive but fragile capabilities of larger command vehicles.

The Browning retains four tons of communications equipment, enough to coordinate regiment-level operations and maintain satellite links without the full battle computer suite of the heavier Mobile HQ. A Guardian ECM Suite provides electronic warfare protection, jamming enemy targeting systems and shielding nearby friendly units from advanced munitions. A McArthur Anti-Missile System offers point defense against incoming missiles, with its ammunition bay protected by CASE to prevent a catastrophic kill if the magazine is breached.

Powered by an Omni 130 fusion engine, the Browning achieves a brisk top speed of 97 km/h, making it one of the fastest command vehicles in service. StarSlab/3 armor provides reasonable protection for a vehicle of its weight class, though commanders are well advised to keep the Browning behind the front lines. The vehicle carries no offensive weaponry, relying entirely on its speed and electronic defenses for survival. The Bowman CommSet with integrated Guardian ECM and Wayne SweepSight targeting system provide a comprehensive electronic picture of the battlefield for the command staff.

The Star League Defense Force fielded thousands of regiments across hundreds of worlds, a military establishment of unprecedented scale. Such forces required extensive command and control infrastructure, from the sophisticated Mobile HQ down to simple command vans. The Browning occupied a middle ground, providing capable field coordination without the complexity and expense of the full-sized Mobile HQ. Mitchell Vehicles of Terra produced the Browning alongside other support vehicles, establishing it as a reliable workhorse of SLDF logistics formations.

The Republic of the Sphere was the primary force behind the Browning's return to the battlefield. Needing greater command capability at every level for its mixed Clan and Inner Sphere force structure, the Republic made the Browning a common sight among its formations. The vehicle proved its worth during the Capellan Crusades and the battles following the Blackout. Following the Republic's contraction, First Prince Julian Davion re-equipped his forces with former Republic supplies, and the Federated Suns became the largest operator of Brownings after the Republic. Further deliveries solidified the Browning's place in AFFS service through the ilClan era. A limited run of Browning Half-Track models was also produced, offering improved rough-terrain mobility at the cost of top speed.

Built in the late 2990s at Kressly WarWorks' Epsilon Eridani facility, the Brutus Assault Tank was designed to give the Capellan Confederation's second-line forces an affordable heavy fire support platform capable of engaging targets at every range. Drawing on established industrial suppliers, Kressly built a practical if unspectacular vehicle that proved more capable in sustained combat than its early garrison assignments suggested. The Fourth Succession War expanded the Brutus's reach far beyond its Capellan origins, and subsequent political changes on Epsilon Eridani brought the design to Federated Commonwealth formations, Chaos March militias, and eventually the Word of Blake Protectorate. By the mid-thirty-first century, the Brutus had become one of the most broadly distributed heavy combat vehicles in the Inner Sphere, proof of both its durability and the longevity of the Kressly production line.

The Brutus carries a balanced weapon suite optimized for flexibility across multiple engagement ranges. Its primary energy weapons deliver direct-fire damage without ammunition dependency, while a long-range missile rack with a generous three-ton ammunition reserve provides sustained fire support capability at extended distances. A pair of short-range missile launchers rounds out the armament for close engagements where opponents press through the long-range envelope. Together, the combination ensures the tank retains offensive options regardless of range, making it difficult for opponents to disengage safely.

Powered by a standard fusion engine, the Brutus achieves modest ground speeds that favor defensive positions and hull-down tactics over open-ground maneuver. Its tracked configuration handles most terrain types without difficulty but limits cross-country speed compared to wheeled or hover designs. The most significant tactical liability is the armor system, which provides considerably less protection than Inner Sphere standards for a vehicle of this mass. Crews compensate through positional discipline, engaging from cover and relying on the missile rack's range to keep more dangerous opponents at a disadvantage.

Kressly WarWorks delivered the first production Brutus Assault Tanks in 2998, fulfilling a Capellan Confederation contract to supply second-line armored formations with an affordable heavy fire support vehicle. Epsilon Eridani had long served as a secondary industrial world in the Confederation's manufacturing network, and the new tank drew on established local suppliers for its major systems. Capellan High Command assigned the Brutus almost exclusively to planetary defense commands and garrison formations, reflecting their low opinion of the design's combat potential.

The Fourth Succession War forced a reassessment. Brutus crews serving in second-line roles demonstrated consistent effectiveness against Federated Suns opponents, and when the war ended with Epsilon Eridani under Federated Commonwealth control, the new administration preserved Kressly WarWorks' production line. The Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth began incorporating the design into Regimental Combat Teams, and Brutus tanks appeared on worlds far from their origin. Early factory variants entered service during this period, tailoring the basic design for specific operational requirements.

The political fragmentation that produced the Chaos March after the Federated Commonwealth's collapse left several Kressly production runs on worlds outside centralized control. Local militias and mercenary commands absorbed those vehicles, and the Brutus became a fixture of Chaos March ground forces. Word of Blake's Protectorate eventually absorbed Epsilon Eridani, bringing Kressly WarWorks under Blake authority. Production increased under Blake direction, and open-market sales ceased as the factory shifted to supplying Blake forces. Brutus tanks were subsequently observed operating in Blake colors across multiple contested worlds during the Jihad.

The Bulldog Medium Tank traces its origins to Bulldog Enterprises, a civilian vehicle manufacturer that sought to expand into the Star League Defense Force market in the twenty-seventh century. Introduced in 2673, the sixty-ton tracked design was conceived as a low-cost, easily maintainable combat vehicle suitable for fielding in battalion and regimental strength without straining the logistics of planetary militias and conventional army formations. While the tank's performance never distinguished itself among competing designs of the era, its competitive price point drove substantial sales, and Bulldog Enterprises licensed production to Quikscell Company on Ares in 2700 to better serve Capellan Confederation markets. The Draconis Combine and Capellan Confederation became the primary operators of the type, and both states continued to adapt and modernize the design across successive eras, producing updated variants suited to the technological capabilities of each period.

The Bulldog is an honest but unexceptional combat vehicle. Its internal combustion engine propels the sixty-ton tracked chassis to a cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour, reaching sixty-four kilometers per hour at maximum effort, placing it within the typical performance envelope of medium tanks of its era without excelling in any particular quality. Bulldog Standard armor provides adequate protection across the hull, sufficient to withstand infantry weapons and light anti-vehicle fire, though it offers no particular advantage against dedicated anti-armor systems.

The primary armament is a single Bulldog large laser, providing reliable energy fire at extended range without ammunition dependency. A pair of Hovertec Quad SRM-4 launchers supplements the laser at shorter distances, adding considerable throw weight during engagements where the enemy has closed within a few hundred meters. A forward-mounted machine gun provides anti-infantry coverage and harassment fire capability.

What the Bulldog lacks in raw performance, it compensates for in mechanical simplicity. Designers deliberately selected standardized, widely available components throughout the vehicle, ensuring technicians can source replacement parts from salvaged hulls across virtually any Inner Sphere battlefield. Many Bulldogs written off as unrecoverable have returned to service under opposing colors within days, a reliable indicator of how interchangeable the design's components have become across the Inner Sphere.

When Bulldog Enterprises introduced its first military vehicle in 2673, the design attracted tepid reviews from procurement officers accustomed to more capable equipment. The tank's armament and protection compared adequately against existing designs but offered nothing to justify displacing established suppliers from lucrative Star League contracts. Sales grew gradually as the company cultivated relationships with planetary militias and low-budget garrison commands, positioning the vehicle as the affordable option for formations that could not justify premium prices. By 2700, Bulldog Enterprises licensed manufacturing rights to Quikscell Company on Ares, establishing a second production center oriented toward Capellan Confederation customers and cementing the Draconis Combine-Capellan industrial partnership that would sustain the design across centuries of conflict.

The Succession Wars fundamentally changed the Bulldog's role in the Inner Sphere order of battle. As more capable designs were destroyed faster than industry could replace them and high-technology components grew increasingly scarce, the tank's manageable maintenance requirements and easily sourced parts transformed from liabilities into genuine advantages. House Davion recognized this reality early, stockpiling large numbers in anticipation of prolonged attrition warfare. Supply eventually proved finite, and by the midpoint of the Third Succession War even Davion reserves had been substantially worn down. Surviving hulks remained repairable long past their expected service lives, however, and the Bulldog persisted across the Inner Sphere's depleted arsenals.

During a major Roughriders raid into Draconis Combine territory at Sternwerde in 3035, Bulldog tanks proved their worth in mass formation operations against a superior defending force. Targeting inbound DropShips during the landing phase, crews using inferno missiles triggered catastrophic detonations among troops and equipment not yet clear of the vessels, destroying three DCMS regiments before they could deploy to the battlefield.

The Capellan production facility on Ares proved difficult to defend during the years following the Fourth Succession War. Successive Davion raids stripped the planet of assembled vehicles and finished stocks, with the defending garrison too demoralized and outmatched to mount effective resistance as long as the raiders avoided the BattleMech repair facilities. Production eventually stabilized, and the Ares plant continued supplying Capellan conventional forces through the Jihad and into the Dark Age period.

Modernization efforts during the Republic era produced the extended-range laser variant, substantially improving the design's firepower and protection. Subsequent modifications by both the Draconis Combine and Capellan Confederation addressed specific operational gaps in their conventional force structures, and by the ilClan era the Bulldog had outlasted contemporaries far more capable on paper, a sign of the enduring value of availability and affordability in sustained conventional warfare.

shared: The Bulwark Assault Vehicle is an eighty-five-ton tracked combat vehicle designed and manufactured by Brooks Incorporated on Kendall for the Free Worlds League. Conceived in 3068 to fill a gap in heavy armor doctrine, the Bulwark pairs devastating long-range direct-fire weapons with exceptional protection to engage and destroy enemy heavy armor formations at distances that keep the vehicle relatively safe from return fire. Production difficulties delayed delivery until 3087, and the design went on to serve with League armor commands and mercenary units across the Inner Sphere. An updated production variant entered service in 3114, incorporating improved weapons and significantly enhanced armor protection, cementing the Bulwark's place as one of the most capable assault vehicles available to Free Worlds League commanders.

The Bulwark's primary armament is an Imperator Titan's Wrath Improved Heavy Gauss Rifle, a weapon capable of striking targets at extreme ranges with penetrating power sufficient to threaten even the most heavily armored opponents. A Fusigon Strongtooth Heavy Particle Projection Cannon provides complementary firepower without the ammunition constraints of ballistic weapons, allowing the crew to sustain fire long after Gauss rifle reserves are depleted. Together, these weapons allow the Bulwark to engage targets across nearly every tactical range band from behind prepared positions or in direct support of advancing armor.

The Durallex Special Heavy Ferro-Fibrous armor provides protection exceeding what most vehicles of comparable weight carry, allowing the Bulwark to absorb multiple direct hits from heavy weapons and remain combat effective. A Strand 340 XL fusion engine provides adequate mobility for a vehicle of its class at a cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour, though the Bulwark is not designed for rapid repositioning. Its Maxell 700 communications suite and Maxell TA92 targeting system are solid, dependable equipment well suited to the vehicle's fire support role. The Bulwark's primary tactical weaknesses are its limited ground speed, which makes it dependent on favorable terrain or well-prepared positions, and the logistical demands of keeping its heavy Gauss rifle ammunition supplied in sustained operations.

The Bulwark originated as a Free Worlds League development program in 3068, conceived to provide heavy armor formations with a tracked vehicle capable of engaging and destroying Clan and advanced Inner Sphere heavy armor at long range. Brooks Incorporated received the design contract and began prototype work at their Kendall facility, but the Jihad's outbreak halted all production planning before a single unit could be manufactured for service. The conflict consumed industrial resources across the League and disrupted supply chains critical to getting the Bulwark into production, and it was not until 3087 that the first operational examples finally left the assembly line.

These early production vehicles served through the late Jihad and into the early Republic era, earning a reputation as a capable if logistically demanding platform. Brooks Incorporated continued refining the design throughout the period, and by 3114 a substantially upgraded production run entered service, replacing the original weapon configuration with more advanced armament and adding heavy ferro-fibrous armor that substantially improved crew survivability. The transition effectively retired the earlier production vehicles from front-line service, with most being cannibalized for components or relegated to garrison roles.

During the Andurien-Oriente War in 3138, a company of Bulwarks under Force Captain Carson Bolling held Tsongas Pass on Deschenes against a Covenant Worlds Expeditionary Force combined-arms battalion. Bolling positioned his vehicles at the narrowest point of the pass and dug in, repelling multiple CWEF assaults over three hours. When the CWEF commander ordered an all-out attack, the Bulwarks concentrated fire on the three heaviest opposing 'Mechs and destroyed them in a single volley. The engagement secured the Third Andurien Guards' hold on Deschenes and earned Bolling a promotion and assignment to the Humphreys Training Academy, where he became an armor doctrine instructor.

The design attracted mercenary interest as well. Hansen's Roughriders' Old Guard armored company operated several Bulwarks, including one of the first 3114-production vehicles off the line, designated Bromhead Remembrance. During the Jade Falcons' assault on Galatea in 3138, two Old Guard Bulwarks held Gilroy Crossing for three hours against sustained Falcon pressure, claiming nine Clan 'Mech kills before Roughrider BattleMechs arrived to relieve the position. The engagement demonstrated the updated Bulwark's lethality in high-intensity combat and raised the vehicle's profile among mercenary employers seeking heavy fire support assets.

The Burke Defense Tank is a seventy-five-ton tracked heavy vehicle developed by Foretechno on Terra in 2575. Designed during the formation of the Star League Defense Force, the Burke addressed the SLDF's urgent need for a heavy fire support platform capable of killing a BattleMech at long range with a single combined salvo from its triple particle cannon battery. Sacrificing mobility for firepower, the Burke became the backbone of SLDF heavy tank regiments throughout the Reunification War and the subsequent garrison operations of the Star League era. Its formidable long-range striking power and durable ferro-fibrous protection made it a feared defender in fixed positions, and its reputation spread even to the Periphery, where enemy commanders learned to route around dug-in Burke formations rather than assault them directly. The design survived the Star League's fall in limited numbers, later serving the Com Guards, the Word of Blake, and Clan Hell's Horses.

Powered by a GM 150 internal combustion engine, the Burke moves slowly for its class but compensates with outstanding firepower at long range. Three Chalker Model 25 particle projection cannons mounted in the turret form the vehicle's primary battery, capable of delivering a coordinated strike that disrupts enemy communications and targeting systems through electromagnetic interference. In extreme cases, this interference can overload a BattleMech's onboard computers. Complementing the main turret is a Holly LRM-10 missile rack that extends the Burke's reach and provides suppression against lighter targets and infantry formations.

Acbar 55 ferro-fibrous armor wraps the hull in protection substantially better than equivalent-mass standard plate, giving the Burke staying power suited to its static defense role. The 1 Division 300 communications system and Scope 30 RNDST targeting array provide reliable electronics appropriate to the vehicle's long-range engagement profile. The Burke's primary weakness is its inability to sustain a prolonged engagement against multiple opponents: against a single BattleMech at range it can hold its own, but poor maneuverability and relatively light armor for its tonnage leave it vulnerable when facing flanking forces or sustained close-range pressure.

Foretechno began development of the Burke at their Maranello works on Terra in 2575, responding to SLDF specifications for a heavy tank capable of matching BattleMech firepower in static defense. Five years of development preceded the first production vehicles entering SLDF service, and full-scale production quickly followed as the Reunification War created intense demand. The Burke became the backbone of SLDF heavy tank regiments within a decade, with many commands fielding entire battalions. Its defensive reputation grew to the point that Periphery commanders began routing operations to bypass dug-in Burke formations rather than assault them frontally.

As the SLDF adopted the highly mobile Striker regiment doctrine, the Burke's limited ground speed made it unsuitable for evolving combined-arms tactics, and it was progressively relegated to garrison duty. Production continued sporadically, but uneven demand caused Foretechno serious financial problems. With thousands of Burkes still in active service, the SLDF Quartermaster Command bought out Foretechno's shareholders in 2755 and restructured the company before transferring its assets to Leopard Armor, which committed to ongoing vehicle support. The Leopard Armor plant on Terra continued production until it was destroyed in 2778.

When the Star League collapsed, surviving Burkes passed to the Inner Sphere successor states, but without Leopard Armor's manufacturing support, few vehicles survived the Succession Wars. The formation of the Com Guards brought the design back into regular Inner Sphere service, and following the ComStar schism, the Word of Blake also adopted the Burke for garrison roles. Among the Clans, the Hell's Horses preserved significant concentrations of Burkes from the SLDF Exodus fleet, maintaining them as heavy armor assets in their touman. The type's long service record reflects both its remarkable defensive capabilities in the right environment and the enduring difficulty of replacing equipment once it has become embedded in institutional logistics.

The Carnivore Assault Tank is an eighty-ton tracked combat vehicle commissioned by Clan Wolf in 3082 as part of a crash program to rebuild the Wolf Touman following the liberation of Terra. Though the Jihad exacted a heavy toll on all Coalition forces, the Wolves recognized that armored vehicles offered a faster and cheaper path to restored combat strength than waiting for new BattleMech production lines to come online. W-7 Facilities on Weingarten received the contract, with scientists directed to maximize component reuse from existing platforms while still producing an effective combat machine. The result is a long-range fire support platform built around twin Gauss rifles and extended-range medium lasers, striking a practical balance between raw firepower and logistical simplicity. Early evaluations from test units indicated the Carnivore succeeded on both counts, though Clan warriors continued to regard armored vehicles with considerably less esteem than BattleMechs or aerospace fighters.

The Carnivore is powered by a 320 XL fusion engine, providing cruising and flank speeds of forty-three and sixty-four kilometers per hour respectively. While not exceptional for an eighty-ton vehicle, its performance compares favorably to many designs of similar mass. The hull mounts Advanced/3 composite armor, which offers slightly less peak protection than ferro-fibrous compounds but is cheaper to manufacture and imposes fewer space constraints on the vehicle's interior. A CASE system is integrated to improve crew survivability in the event of a catastrophic ammunition detonation.

Two Series II Gauss Rifles form the heart of the Carnivore's offensive capability. These are the same model fitted to the Sun Cobra BattleMech, a deliberate procurement decision that simplified logistics by consolidating the supply chain. With excellent range and hard-hitting kinetics, the rifles give the tank a reliable long-range engagement profile, though the thirty-two round ammunition supply demands careful fire discipline. A pair of Series 2d ER Medium Lasers supplements the main guns at intermediate ranges, providing sustained fire capability without drawing on the Gauss stockpile. Two Series XIV Heavy Machine Guns round out the armament for close-in defense against infantry. The 2SH C3 communications system incorporates an integral ECM suite, supporting network warfare and providing countermeasures against opposing electronic systems, while the Build 4 JVJ targeting and tracking system ties the weapons array together into a coherent fire control solution.

The Carnivore's development traces directly to the damage the Jihad inflicted on Clan Wolf's military assets. The campaign against the Word of Blake's Protectorate and the siege of Terra cost the Wolves heavily in equipment and personnel. While the Clan hierarchy focused its rebuilding efforts on BattleMech and aerospace fighter production, practical military planners recognized that armored vehicles offered a faster and cheaper path to restored combat strength. The traditional Clan disdain for combat vehicles had long kept the armor arm underprioritized, but necessity overrode tradition in the years after 3081.

W-7 Facilities on Weingarten received the Carnivore contract with specific instructions to minimize costs and manufacturing complexity by maximizing component reuse from existing Clan Wolf platforms. The scientists involved drew the communications suite from the Ares, a Clan Wolf vehicle with an established second-line service record, and sourced the main guns from the same production run supplying the Sun Cobra. The design entered limited service in mid-3082, initially assigned to shore up frontline formations temporarily short on BattleMech assets, with the open market version following as variants became available.

Despite meeting their design objectives, Carnivore crews operated in the shadow of the Clan warrior caste's cultural hierarchy. Armor crews never commanded the battlefield respect accorded to MechWarriors or aerospace pilots, and the tank's fire support role kept it in a supporting rather than starring capacity in most engagements. That cultural ambivalence did not prevent the design from filling a genuine operational need, and the Carnivore carved out a reliable place in the Wolf Touman's order of battle through the Dark Age. The success of the basic chassis prompted development of both a trade variant for Clan Jade Falcon and a simplified second-line version for broader commercial distribution. When Weingarten passed from Clan Wolf into Clan Hell's Horses control, the Horses continued production of the Carnivore family, finding the design well-suited to their own combined-arms doctrine.

The Cavalry Attack Helicopter is a 25-ton VTOL assault craft developed by Michaelson Heavy Industries and first produced at Ruchbah in 3054. Designed as a rapid relief and assault platform, the helicopter was intended for hit-and-run operations against armored targets, and it quickly became one of the most capable strike helicopters in the AFFC inventory within its first decade of service. Early production runs were acquired primarily by AFFC units and noble houses of the Draconis March and Sarna March, while a substantial portion reached mercenary operators concentrated in the Chaos March. The Cavalry's sturdy airframe proved adaptable enough to support multiple specialized variants across its production life. Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion at Belladonna later developed advanced stealth-equipped configurations for Federated Suns intelligence and rapid-deployment operations. Licensed production spread further during the Dark Age, with Kallon Weapon Industries and Yan Manufacturing extending the design's reach across multiple successor states.

The base Cavalry combines a Harpoon SRM-6 rack with three Holly SRM-2 launchers, delivering a dozen short-range missile tubes from a fast-moving airframe. Cruising at 108 kph with a flank speed of 162 kph, pilots strike from concealed positions or attack from the rear before breaking off before the enemy can respond effectively. This tactic is particularly effective against armored vehicles and tanks, the helicopter's primary targets. The Michaelson 110 internal combustion engine provides reliable performance, while StarSlab/3 armor applied to the nose section allows the Cavalry to absorb hits from weapons as powerful as a Clan PPC or Gauss rifle and remain airborne. Garret Supremesound and Garret D2j electronics handle communications and targeting duties across most production variants.

The design's primary limitation is ammunition supply. With no backup weapons, crews must exercise strict fire discipline, as exhausting the missile bays leaves the helicopter defenseless in extended engagements. Like all VTOLs, the rotor system is a critical vulnerability, though Michaelson reinforced it as heavily as the weight budget permitted.

Later variants significantly expanded the design's capabilities. The infantry support model replaces the internal combustion engine with a fusion powerplant and trades missile armament for medium lasers, machine guns, and a troop bay sized for a full infantry platoon. Advanced Cal-Boeing configurations add vehicular stealth armor and VTOL jet boosters for covert insertion operations, while an experimental prototype incorporated a Guardian ECM suite and chin-mounted Magshot Gauss rifles.

Michaelson Heavy Industries introduced the Cavalry in 3054 as part of a new line of rapid assault VTOLs designed for the post-Clan Invasion battlefield. Early production was acquired primarily by AFFC units and noble houses of the Draconis March and Sarna March for personal guard allocations. A substantial mercenary market developed quickly, concentrated among the many small commands operating across the Chaos March, most working for FedCom-loyal factions. The helicopter's hunter-killer reputation was established through these early deployments, where its speed and firepower made it effective against the armored threats that proliferated through the conflict-saturated region.

The FedCom Civil War brought the Cavalry to wider attention. On Talon, the Seventh FedCom RCT fought at great cost through mountain valleys to prevent the Twenty-Second Avalon Hussars from reaching orbit and reinforcing Loyalist defenses on New Avalon. The Cavalry's speed and firepower proved decisive in breaking through armored positions that conventional ground forces struggled to force. That performance cemented the helicopter's reputation across both sides of the conflict and accelerated demand among regular military and mercenary operators alike.

Control of Ruchbah passed through several occupiers during the Jihad, including a period under Word of Blake administration that disrupted established supply chains. After the Jihad, the facility operated under Republic of the Sphere oversight before transitioning through independent control and eventually into Capellan Confederation hands across the Dark Age.

Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion pursued a separate development path at Belladonna, producing the experimental CADENCE RAIN prototype in 3075 as a covert battle armor delivery platform. Severe limitations in vehicular stealth armor supply restricted production to a handful of airframes, and the death of the program director during a test flight set development back nearly two years. The experience gained fed directly into the more capable Infiltrator, which entered full production in 3085 and became a priority asset for Federated Suns intelligence operations. Michaelson's declining financial position drove licensing arrangements in the same period, bringing Kallon Weapon Industries and Yan Manufacturing into the production network and extending the Cavalry's operational reach across the Dark Age Inner Sphere.

The Centipede Scout Car is a twenty-ton hover reconnaissance vehicle developed by Gienah Combat Vehicles in the early 3050s to address a critical gap in the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces' light reconnaissance inventory. Designed as a replacement for the aging Skulker Wheeled Scout Tank following the loss of that design's primary production source, the Centipede represented a significant advance in light recon vehicle design, trading a wheeled platform's durability for dramatic improvements in speed, firepower, and sensor capability. Gienah Combat Vehicles partnered with Red Devil Industries of Pandora to expand production capacity, and the Centipede quickly became the standard scout vehicle across LAAF front-line formations and planetary militia units alike. Its combination of high speed, advanced detection equipment, and respectable armament for its weight class established the design as one of the Inner Sphere's most capable purpose-built reconnaissance vehicles of its era.

The Centipede Scout Car's defining strength is its exceptional speed. Powered by a VOX Type 75 internal combustion engine, the vehicle reaches a flank speed of 129 kilometers per hour, allowing it to outpace most comparable scout designs in its weight class. This speed serves as the Centipede's primary defensive asset, enabling rapid repositioning and withdrawal under fire that few adversaries can match.

Its nose-mounted Beagle Active Probe is the vehicle's most valuable battlefield asset. The system detects concealed units at ranges exceeding those of many BattleMech-mounted sensor suites and provides targeting guidance to the Defiance B3M medium laser, enhancing acquisition accuracy against moving targets to a standard matching the most advanced fire control systems available. A Zippo vehicular flamer mounted at the rear supplements the primary armament, functioning as an effective anti-infantry tool and giving crews the means to cover withdrawal by igniting terrain.

The ProtecTech 6 armor suite provides modest but adequate protection for a light reconnaissance design, requiring crews to rely on speed and sensor advantage rather than direct engagement to survive on the modern battlefield. The Scuti Dualcom communications system and Scuti Dualtar targeting system give the Centipede reliable battlefield networking capability, making it an effective intelligence node in combined-arms formations that depend on accurate and timely reconnaissance data.

The Centipede Scout Car emerged from disruptions caused by the Clan Invasion. When Clan Ghost Bear overran Joint Equipment Systems' production facilities in 3051, the Skulker Wheeled Scout Tank lost its primary manufacturing source, leaving the Lyran Alliance short of capable light reconnaissance vehicles. Gienah Combat Vehicles responded by developing the Centipede as a purpose-built hover replacement, introducing the design in 3054. To meet growing LAAF demand, Gienah partnered with Red Devil Industries of Pandora as a second production partner, establishing two manufacturing lines for the new scout vehicle.

The design proved its value during the FedCom Civil War and the renewed Jade Falcon Incursion into Lyran space, where its speed and detection capabilities provided meaningful intelligence advantages to Lyran commanders. The Jade Falcons recognized the threat and made deliberate efforts to destroy Centipede units wherever encountered, reportedly dedicating screening forces to locating and eliminating the vehicles. When Pandora fell to Clan Jade Falcon's Rho Galaxy in 3064, Red Devil Industries was captured and production at that facility ceased.

The Jihad dealt the surviving production line a severe blow. In September 3068, mercenary forces believed to be operating on behalf of House Marik raided Gienah, striking the Gienah Combat Vehicles facility at Molfetta and inflicting serious damage on the production lines. The assault spread to neighboring Gienah Automotive plants when workers from those facilities joined the confrontation, compounding the industrial damage. These events generated lasting resentment toward the Free Worlds League among Gienah's population, who had maintained an informal non-aggression arrangement with the League since the Second Succession War.

Despite the loss of both production lines, the Centipede's story continued. Gienah Combat Vehicles pursued legal action against Red Devil Industries after discovering the company had been distributing Centipedes through black market channels on Galatea. Production eventually resumed on Pandora after Merchant Factor Daniel's rise in 3070, continuing in an advanced configuration under Jade Falcon oversight. On Inarcs, ScolTek Associates R&D unveiled an experimental development based on the original chassis in 3074, producing limited numbers before the close of the Jihad period.

text.capabilities:
The AC/2 Carrier mounts five forward-firing Class 2 autocannons as its sole armament, a configuration that emphasizes sustained long-range harassment over decisive striking power. One hundred and eighty rounds of ammunition provide substantial endurance for extended fire missions, allowing the vehicle to maintain suppressive fire far longer than its missile carrier cousins. An InterComBust 180 internal combustion engine propels the vehicle to a maximum speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour.

Three tons of Simple Armor Plate Standard provide minimal protection, making the AC/2 Carrier as vulnerable as any other member of the weapons carrier family. A Communicator system and FireScan with IndirecTrack handle targeting and coordination. The AC/2 Carrier's primary tactical advantage lies in its extreme range and ammunition endurance, allowing it to engage from standoff distances where return fire is less accurate.
text.deployment: The AC/2 Carrier serves in most major militaries across the Inner Sphere, typically deployed in fire support lances providing long-range suppressive fire. Its extreme engagement range and ammunition endurance make it particularly effective in defensive positions where sustained harassment of approaching forces is more valuable than decisive firepower. The vehicle has been frequently confused with the Pike support vehicle in after-action reports due to their comparable size and armament.
text.battleHistory:
The AC/2 Carrier traces its lineage to the Age of War, when Quik Products Inc developed a family of standardized tracked weapons platforms. The primitive ancestor entered service around 2520 mounting four Class 2 autocannons behind BAR 6 armor with advanced fire control systems. Despite crude construction, the design proved effective enough to inspire the modernized version that served through the Star League era and beyond. Like the missile carriers, the AC/2 Carrier suffered from widespread unauthorized copying during the Succession Wars, and Quikscell's post-Fourth Succession War legal campaign shut down many competitors.

Production spread across an extensive network. Quikscell plants on Ares, Kalidasa, Layover, Oliver, Pandora, and Richvale formed the core, supplemented by Hadrian Mechanized Industries on Pompey, Aldis Industries on Terra, Bordello Military Goods on Antwerp, and Joint Equipment Systems on Alshain. This distributed base mirrored the missile carrier network.

The AC/2 Carrier received its first major modernization in 3063 with the LB-X variant. This substantial redesign replaced the internal combustion engine with a fusion powerplant, doubled armor protection, and substituted the standard autocannons with LB-X Class 2 weapons capable of firing both solid slugs and cluster ammunition. A C3 slave computer enabled networked targeting. Quikscell produced the LB-X variant at most of its carrier plants.

Despite its long service history, the AC/2 Carrier has always occupied a somewhat ambiguous position within the weapons carrier family. The vehicle's similarity to the Pike support vehicle has caused persistent identification problems in the field. Still, the AC/2 Carrier continues to fill its role as cheap long-range suppressive fire support, its simplicity and low cost ensuring continued relevance.

Armor protection doubled to eighty-eight points of standard plating, distributed evenly across all facing arcs. A C3 slave computer enables networked targeting with friendly units, dramatically improving accuracy when operating as part of an integrated company. The combination of upgraded firepower, improved protection, and networked electronics makes the LB-X variant a considerably more capable platform than its predecessor.
text.deployment: The LB-X variant entered service in 3063, just prior to the FedCom Civil War. Quikscell produced it at five of its six carrier plants, with Hadrian Mechanized Industries and Aldis Industries also tooling up for the upgraded model. The cluster ammunition capability proved particularly valuable in the anti-aircraft role, supplementing dedicated air defense assets.

text.deployment: Introduced exclusively to the Duchy of Andurien's military in 3082, the primary Aeron remained unavailable outside Andurien for its first two years of production. When Brooks opened broader sales in 3084, they restricted this version to the Republic of the Sphere and the Duchy of Andurien, citing the ongoing Federated Suns legal dispute over targeting computer technology. Andurien formations deploy it as a precision fire support platform, exploiting its speed and standoff accuracy to destroy light armor and harass BattleMechs from advantageous range. Republic forces use it in screening and reconnaissance-in-force roles, pairing its ECM capability with its long-range strike power. Federated Suns units have taken to field refitting BAP variants with locally produced targeting computers, bypassing the sales restriction through technical means rather than commercial channels.

The BAP variant is the version available to the broader market, trading the targeting computer for a Beagle Active Probe and a half-ton cargo bay. The cargo bay sees frequent use for stowing remote drone equipment, extending the Aeron's reconnaissance and area denial roles beyond direct combat engagement. Active Probe capability adds utility against hidden and shutdown units, making this version well-suited to screening and counterreconnaissance missions that the primary version cannot directly support. This variant has sold widely across the Inner Sphere, with orders arriving from operators in former Hell's Horses territory through Diamond Shark intermediary brokers. Despite lacking the precision of the primary version, the BAP remains the more commonly encountered Aeron in service outside Andurien and the Republic of the Sphere.

The standard Aesir serves as the primary anti-aircraft platform in Clan Wolf and Wolf Empire garrison formations, where full Stars are typically assigned to defend installations, supply depots, and command centers against airborne raids. Its distribution expanded following the Exiled Wolves' acquisition of the production plans in 3101 and Clan Sea Fox's subsequent sale of vehicles to the Republic of the Sphere. The design's straightforward maintenance requirements and ammunition efficiency make it a preferred choice for second-line units that must sustain defensive operations with limited logistical support.

The HAG variant was developed by Clan Hell's Horses following their absorption of Weingarten and the W-7 Facilities that had previously manufactured the base model under Clan Wolf ownership. Replacing the four LB 2-X Autocannons with a single HAG/40, this configuration trades the saturating flak coverage of the original for concentrated firepower better suited to operations in smaller detachments or individual vehicle deployments. Six tons of ammunition feed the larger weapon, but the increased consumption rate makes the HAG variant less suited to the extended engagements for which the base model was designed.

text.overview: The Aithon Assault Transport is a hundred-ton tracked assault vehicle developed by Swedenborg Heavy Industries on Kirchbach for Clan Hell's Horses, entering service in 3084. Conceived as a dedicated heavy infantry transport with significant direct-fire capability, the Aithon was designed to replace several aging vehicle platforms that the Horses could no longer source from the Clan Homeworlds. Its combination of heavy protection, substantial troop-carrying capacity, and devastating artillery firepower has made it a valued asset within the Clan's combined-arms formations. The vehicle fills a critical niche in the Hell's Horses' combat doctrine, where conventional vehicles and infantry operate alongside BattleMechs and Elementals as integral components of assault operations rather than mere support elements.
text.capabilities:
The Aithon's 300-rated extralight fusion engine delivers a modest top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, sacrificing raw speed for the weight savings needed to mount heavy weapons and thick armor on the hundred-ton chassis. The engine's nearly unlimited operating range ensures the transport can sustain extended offensive operations without concern for fuel logistics. A ten-ton infantry bay can accommodate a full Point of standard Elementals, two Points of lighter battle armor, or an equivalent mass of conventional troops and equipment.

Protection is among the Aithon's greatest strengths. Twelve and a half tons of Composite Alpha-V1 ferro-lamellor armor effectively negates the damage potential of lighter weapons and cluster munitions while reducing the impact of heavier strikes by up to twenty percent. An armored motive system adds further resilience, shielding the tracked propulsion from disabling hits that would otherwise leave the vehicle immobilized.

The forward-mounted Model LT-Max Long Tom artillery cannon serves as the Aithon's primary weapon, carrying three tons of CASE-protected ammunition for sustained bombardment of bunkers, fortifications, and prepared positions. Four turret-mounted Series 14a medium pulse lasers provide accurate close-in defense, covering the vehicle during the vulnerable process of loading and unloading its infantry complement.
text.deployment:
Given its limited ground speed and assault transport role, the Aithon is not a front-line combat vehicle in the traditional sense. Field commanders instead deploy it wherever the Hell's Horses are determined to assault a position or break through entrenched resistance. The presence of an Aithon in a Horses formation does not necessarily indicate an imminent infantry assault, however. Some Periphery operations have seen these vehicles repurposed as salvage transports or prisoner wagons, their heavy armor and firepower first employed to overwhelm the opposition before their cargo bays are put to alternative use.

To date, all Aithons manufactured at Swedenborg Heavy Industries have been distributed among the Hell's Horses' various assault Clusters, where their limited mobility is offset by the near-constant presence of supporting BattleMechs and vehicles.
text.battleHistory:
Swedenborg Heavy Industries has a long and varied history predating its association with Clan Hell's Horses. Originally a struggling IndustrialMech manufacturer under Draconis Combine ownership, the facility saw its fortunes improve dramatically after the formation of the Free Rasalhague Republic, when output more than tripled. A BattleMech construction wing was under development when Clan Wolf seized Kirchbach during the initial Clan Invasion, leaving the project unfinished. Under Wolf stewardship, the plant shifted to producing ballistic and missile weapons.

The Hell's Horses acquired Kirchbach during their invasion of the Wolf Occupation Zone, and the Clan wasted no time capitalizing on Swedenborg's potential. Cut off from their regular supply lines to the Homeworlds, the Horses invested heavily in modernizing the facility, establishing new production lines for engines, armor, energy weapons, and electronics alongside vehicle and battle armor manufacturing capabilities. The plant suffered no personnel losses during the Jihad and was operating at ninety-five percent capacity by 3079.

One of the first successes of this renovation effort was the Zephyros infantry support vehicle, a lightweight wheeled design built for fast fire support and intended to replace the Clan's venerable Odin and Mithras light tanks. The Aithon followed as a heavier complement, designed to fill the roles previously held by the Indra infantry transport and the Oro assault vehicle. Where the Zephyros emphasized speed and flexibility, the Aithon prioritized protection and firepower, giving Horses commanders a dedicated platform capable of delivering troops directly into contested areas under its own considerable fire support. No variants have entered production, though speculation about alternative weapon configurations has been fueled by the Horses' ongoing efforts to further expand the Swedenborg factory complex.

text.deployment: Introduced in 3078 to support amphibious operations, the Sealed configuration features environmental sealing that allows the Ajax to operate in underwater and hostile atmospheric conditions. Its armament combines an ER large laser and MML launcher with medium pulse lasers and an SRT launcher for submarine defense, backed by CASE protection and the standard C3 slave and Guardian ECM suite.

The A configuration replaces the Prime's mixed armament with three rotary autocannons, delivering devastating volumes of fire at the cost of increased ammunition dependency. A Guardian ECM suite provides electronic warfare protection, making this the preferred choice for crews operating in environments where enemy electronic warfare is a concern. It remains one of the most popular Ajax configurations in frontline service.

Configured as a command and fire support vehicle, the B configuration mounts three LRM launchers paired with Artemis IV fire control systems and a PPC for direct-fire capability. A C3 master computer replaces the slave unit found in other configurations, allowing an Ajax B crew to coordinate the fire of an entire lance or company from a heavily armored platform.
text.battleHistory:
The Ajax entered service in 3065, arriving at a decisive moment during the FedCom Civil War. General Motors developed the design following the success of its Challenger X main battle tank, recognizing that the OmniVehicle concept pioneered by Star Corps' Manteuffel could be applied to heavier platforms. Production was established across three Federated Suns worlds, with General Motors facilities on Kathil and Salem joined by the GM/Blackwell Industries partnership on New Valencia.

The first Ajax tanks off the production lines on Kathil were assigned to the Fifth Davion Guards and Sixth Syrtis Fusiliers RCTs, units that put them to immediate use in their fight against the Eighth FedCom RCT and the Eighth Donegal Guards on New Syrtis. The Ajax proved its worth in these engagements, demonstrating the flexibility that the OmniVehicle concept promised. After the Fifth Davion Guards was officially deactivated following their victory, Leftenant General Seth Varnay led a mixed force that included a significant number of Ajax tanks to New Avalon, where their firepower was again put to effective use.

By the end of the Civil War, the Ajax had become a fixture in Federated Suns armored units. Nearly every surviving armored formation that fought with an RCT in the war retained Ajax tanks in its inventory. Production continued through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, with all three factory lines maintaining active output. The Kathil facility later expanded its production to include the environmentally sealed variant designed for amphibious assault missions, broadening the Ajax's operational envelope considerably. The design's enduring popularity reflected both its robust construction and the practical advantages of OmniVehicle technology for logistics-conscious commanders.

text.deployment: Introduced during the opening stages of the Jihad in 3068, the C configuration emphasizes close-range lethality. A targeting computer enhances its turret-mounted PPC, while four Streak SRM launchers and a bow-mounted MRM launcher deliver punishing short-range salvos. A Guardian ECM suite rounds out the electronics package.
