A targeting computer enhances its turret-mounted PPC, while four Streak SRM launchers and a bow-mounted MRM launcher deliver punishing short-range salvos. A Guardian ECM suite rounds out the electronics package, providing protection against Jihad-era electronic warfare threats.

The Prime configuration represents the Ajax's baseline combat loadout, combining direct-fire ballistic weapons with close-range backup systems. Its mix of a Gauss rifle and Ultra Autocannon gives crews flexibility against both heavily armored and lighter targets, while C3 slave integration makes it particularly effective in coordinated lance operations. This configuration sees the widest deployment across Federated Suns armored units.

The Mk I was one of two original prototypes submitted to the Terran Hegemony Armed Forces in 2561. Armed with three Class 10 autocannons and clad in prototype ferro-fibrous armor, it demonstrated formidable firepower but was ultimately rejected after extensive trials revealed persistent armor manufacturing defects. No production run followed, and surviving examples are exceedingly rare museum pieces.

The Mk II prototype was developed alongside the Mk I, sharing the same engine and chassis but replacing the autocannon battery with three Class 20 models. While this gave the tank devastating close-range punch, the severe reduction in armor protection to just six tons made the design impractical for the close engagements its weapons demanded. The Hegemony Armed Forces rejected it, and the Mk II never entered production.

production.manufacturer: Corben Motors, New Earth Trading Company

text.deployment: The Mk III was the first production variant of the Alacorn, incorporating an extralight engine and retaining the Mk I's triple Class 10 autocannon armament. Produced initially by Corben Motors and later by NETC after the acquisition, the Mk III served with the SLDF in limited numbers. It was largely superseded once the Mk VI entered service, though examples lingered in garrison formations throughout the Star League era.

The Mk IV paired the Mk III's extralight engine with the Mk II's devastating triple Class 20 autocannon payload, creating a close-range assault vehicle of fearsome power. Produced in small numbers alongside the Mk III, it saw limited service with SLDF units that valued raw stopping power over sustained engagement range. Like the Mk III, it was eventually overshadowed by the gauss-armed Mk VI.

The Mk VI is the definitive and most widely recognized variant of the Alacorn, mounting three gauss rifles that give it unmatched long-range firepower for a vehicle of its class. It served extensively with the SLDF throughout the Periphery before production halted during the Second Succession War. Reintroduced in 3055, the Mk VI is deployed with Davion, Lyran, and mercenary forces throughout the Inner Sphere, with smaller numbers in Combine, Capellan, and Clan service.

Developed in 3063 following the Alacorn's return to production, the Mk VII replaces the standard gauss rifle battery with a pair of Defiance Hammerfist Heavy Gauss Rifles, each fed by six tons of ammunition. This configuration trades the Mk VI's volume of fire for even greater per-shot destructive potential, making the Mk VII one of the hardest-hitting conventional vehicles in the Inner Sphere. It sees service primarily with Lyran and allied forces.

text.overview: The Anat is a twenty-five ton wheeled armored personnel carrier designed by Clan Hell's Horses and first produced in 3092 at Swedenborg Heavy Industries on Kirchbach. Named for an ancient Semitic war goddess, the vehicle was conceived to serve the Horses' combined-arms doctrine by delivering infantry rapidly across varied terrain. The Anat fills a tactical niche between heavier tracked transports and faster but more terrain-limited hovercraft, offering a balance of speed and cross-country capability that has proven appealing well beyond its originating Clan. Extensive trade through Clan Sea Fox merchant networks and direct exchanges with Clan Wolf-in-Exile has spread the Anat throughout the Inner Sphere, making it one of the most widely distributed Clan-origin vehicles of the Dark Age period.
text.capabilities:
Powered by a Fuel Cell 180 engine, the Anat achieves a maximum speed of 129 kilometers per hour, making it one of the faster armored transports in service. Its wheeled chassis provides superior cross-country performance compared to hovercraft when operating in broken or wooded terrain, while limited amphibious equipment allows the vehicle to ford rivers and shallow waterways without difficulty. These qualities make the Anat well suited for keeping attached infantry at the forefront of rapidly advancing formations.

Protection comes from three and a half tons of "Magnum" Ferro-Fibrous Composite armor, sufficient to shrug off small arms fire and light weapons but inadequate against sustained 'Mech-scale engagement. Offensive armament consists of only two turret-mounted Raid Micro Pulse Lasers, effective against unarmored infantry and soft targets but posing little threat to vehicles or BattleMechs. The five-ton infantry bay can accommodate a standard infantry platoon. These limitations mean the Anat requires escort from heavier combat assets when operating near active battlefields, a trade-off the Horses accept in exchange for its speed and versatility.
text.deployment: Anats are found in nearly every garrison and second-line Cluster of Clan Hell's Horses, and regularly deploy with frontline Clusters that embraced the original pre-Malvina Mongol doctrine. They are also widely distributed around the Inner Sphere, with Clan Sea Fox acting as middlemen for Republic and mercenary purchasers. The Horses conduct their own direct trade with the Wolves-in-Exile, who have also procured Anats for their Lyran hosts. The Capellan occupation of much of the rimward Republic has brought large numbers of these APCs into Capellan hands as well.
text.battleHistory:
The Anat entered service during a period of significant expansion for the Hell's Horses, who had recently consolidated their occupation zone in former Clan Wolf territories of the Inner Sphere. Preliminary testing of the vehicle was assigned to Omega Galaxy over the course of 3094 to 3095. On Botany Bay, the Horses stumbled across a hidden base belonging to the notorious buccaneer Black Kat. Anats from the Fifth Rangers Cluster were ordered to race infantry ahead to seize the facility and prevent the pirate's escape. With support from a Star of Eponas, the Anats flanked the pirate force on the flatlands of the Solander peninsula.

Defenses at the base were rudimentary, as it had been established to conceal a Union-class DropShip rather than withstand a Clan assault. The escorting Eponas breached the outer works, and one Anat raced through the ensuing chaos to deliver its infantry Star into the loading bay of the Union. The Clan infantry quickly seized control from within, only to discover that a lance of the pirate's 'Mechs had broken away from the fighting. The Anats formed up with the surviving Eponas to charge the fleeing lance. One Anat crashed into a Fire Moth, disabling the 'Mech at the cost of the vehicle's destruction. The remaining Anats swarmed over Black Kat's own Cougar but were cut down by energy weapons fire. The charge bought time for the Clan infantry to prepare, and their resulting ambushes destroyed the last of the lance as it attempted to retake the base. The contribution of the Anats impressed the Clan leadership sufficiently to authorize full production.

Clan Sea Fox learned of the battle shortly afterward and, following Black Kat's demise, issued a Trial over an Anat prototype to evaluate its potential as an export to the Inner Sphere. The Foxes won narrowly in a hard but honorable fight in which two Anat prototypes were claimed as isorla. Shortly afterward the Fox merchant caste began negotiating a commercial contract with the Horses, opening the trade networks that would eventually spread the vehicle across the Inner Sphere.

One of the prototypes taken as isorla became something of a legend in its own right. Sardonically nicknamed "Passport" after its present commander Si-ben-bing Linda Martov, this particular Anat has repeatedly switched hands since the Blackout. Originally sold to the Republic by the Sea Foxes, it was seized by the Steel Wolves on their formation, then subsequently salvaged by the Highlanders, the Dragon's Fury, and the Stormhammers in turn. It was later traded to the Swordsworn before being captured by the Capellan Armed Forces on Tikonov. How long it remains with the First Tikonov Guards has become the subject of a battalion-wide betting pool.

text.deployment: All Clans use the standard Anhur as their primary planetside logistics transport, moving supplies and equipment from DropShip landing zones to forward units across all terrain types. Clans Blood Spirit, Hell's Horses, and Star Adder permanently assign it to combat formations as an infantry carrier. Clans Fire Mandrill, Goliath Scorpion, Ice Hellion, and Snow Raven employ it in an infantry transport role on an ad hoc basis only.

The BA variant was fielded during the Jihad era by Clan forces requiring a dedicated infantry assault transport with better survivability in contested electronic warfare environments. Its expanded ten-ton infantry bay and ECM suite make it a preferred choice for insertion missions into defended positions. The revised armament of paired ER medium lasers and AP Gauss Rifles covering both forward and rear arcs allows the craft to suppress opposition during approach and withdrawal, though it remains dependent on escort assets when operating against heavier threats.

text.capabilities:
The Ares fields three complementary weapon systems. The primary weapon is a Series 7Ja Extended Range Large Laser mounted in the turret, providing accurate long-range fire with no ammunition dependency. Hull-mounted armament consists of a Type X "Short Bow" LRM-10 and a Type XV "Crossbow" LRM-15, each equipped with an Artemis IV Fire Control System that improves cluster hit accuracy. The missile launchers can deliver indirect fire with spotter support, allowing the crew to engage targets masked by terrain. Clantech guidance packages arm at close range, making the missiles effective even against enemies who press the engagement - a meaningful advantage over Inner Sphere equivalents. Limited missile ammunition forces most crews to rely primarily on the laser, using the missile racks as situational supplements rather than primary weapons.

Four and a half tons of Compound G5 Ferro-Fibrous armor protects the hull and its three-man crew, a modest allocation that reinforces the design's preference for standoff engagement over sustained close combat. CASE protects the ammunition bays, giving crews a reasonable chance of survival in the event of a catastrophic internal explosion. The Ares cruises at 54 km/h and can push to a maximum of 86 km/h, competitive for a fire support vehicle of its class.
text.deployment: The standard Ares serves across most major Clans in garrison and fire support roles, most commonly fielded in second-line Stars alongside battle armor and conventional infantry. The tank provides long-range fire suppression while faster elements close with the enemy. Clan Coyote and Clan Wolf have historically maintained the deepest inventories. Following the Clan Invasion, significant numbers accompanied occupying forces into the Inner Sphere, where the vehicle adapted readily to occupation garrison duty. By the ilClan era the design remained present across multiple Clans despite the elimination of several production lines.

text.deployment: The Plasma variant is produced at the Weingarten facility in Clan Wolf's Occupation Zone, entering service during the Jihad. Replacing the extended-range laser with a plasma cannon and adding a second fifteen-tube missile launcher, the variant is designed to deter enemy BattleMechs from closing with Ares formations. The plasma cannon's ability to impose heat on targets makes it especially effective against high-heat designs attempting to engage at close range. Like the standard model it serves primarily in a garrison role. Control of Weingarten transferred to Clan Hell's Horses after the Jihad, who continued producing the variant through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era.

text.capabilities:
The LRM variant of the hover APC replaces the infantry compartment and turret-mounted machine guns with a forward-firing LRM-5 launcher and one ton of missile ammunition. This conversion entirely eliminates the vehicle's troop-carrying capability, transforming it from a transport into a light fire support platform capable of engaging targets at long range. Twenty-four points of standard armor distributed evenly across all facings provide slightly better protection than the base model's turret-concentrated layout.

Operating at the same maximum speed of over one hundred sixty kilometers per hour, the LRM hover variant retains the platform's characteristic mobility advantage. Militia and garrison commands frequently employ this conversion to provide indirect fire support where dedicated missile carriers are unavailable, using the hover APC's speed to reposition between salvos and avoid counterbattery fire.
text.deployment: The LRM conversion sees widespread use among militia and garrison forces that lack dedicated fire support vehicles. The hover chassis's speed allows LRM-equipped APCs to operate as highly mobile skirmishers, firing missile salvos at long range before relocating to avoid return fire. Many commands field mixed formations of standard and LRM hover APCs, with the missile variants providing overwatch as the transports deliver infantry.

text.capabilities:
The machine gun variant of the hover APC removes the infantry compartment entirely to mount three turret-mounted machine guns, creating a dedicated anti-infantry and anti-soft-target platform. With no troop-carrying capacity, this conversion serves purely as a light combat vehicle rather than a transport. The third machine gun and full ton of ammunition provide sustained anti-personnel firepower from the turret's three-hundred-sixty-degree arc of fire.

Carrying twenty-four points of standard armor and maintaining the hover APC's maximum speed of over one hundred sixty kilometers per hour, this variant excels at running down unprotected infantry and light vehicles in open terrain. Its role overlaps significantly with light scout hovercraft, and many commands prefer purpose-built designs for the anti-infantry role.
text.deployment: The machine gun hover APC serves primarily with planetary security forces and garrison commands for anti-infantry patrol duties. Its combination of speed and concentrated machine gun fire makes it effective for suppressing unarmored insurgent forces, though it offers little value against armored targets. Some mercenary commands use MG hover APCs as scout vehicles in low-threat environments.

text.capabilities:
The sensor variant of the hover APC replaces the turret-mounted machine guns with a remote sensor dispenser while retaining one ton of infantry carrying capacity for a single squad. Designed for reconnaissance and border patrol duties, this configuration allows the vehicle to deploy a network of remote sensors across a wide area while using its exceptional speed to cover vast stretches of terrain. The sensor package transforms the basic transport into a capable intelligence-gathering platform.

Originally developed for the Taurian Concordat and Marian Hegemony for monitoring their extensive Periphery borders, the sensor hover APC proved equally useful to Inner Sphere militaries for forward screening and area denial operations. The vehicle's twenty-four points of standard armor and speed of over one hundred sixty kilometers per hour allow it to perform its reconnaissance mission with reasonable survivability, though the lack of offensive weapons means it must rely entirely on speed to avoid engagement.
text.deployment: The sensor hover APC sees its heaviest use with the Taurian Concordat and Marian Hegemony, where both nations deploy it extensively for border patrol and surveillance along their vast Periphery frontiers. Inner Sphere militaries have adopted the design for forward screening and area denial operations, using the vehicle's speed to rapidly deploy sensor networks across wide areas before withdrawing to safe positions.

text.capabilities:
The SRM variant of the hover APC replaces the turret-mounted machine guns with a forward-firing SRM-2 launcher while retaining one ton of infantry carrying capacity for a single squad. This gives the vehicle modest anti-armor capability alongside its transport role, allowing it to engage light vehicles and BattleMech rear armor while still fulfilling its primary mission of delivering infantry to the combat zone. One ton of SRM ammunition provides adequate endurance for most operations.

Twenty-four points of standard armor and the characteristic hover speed of over one hundred sixty kilometers per hour allow the SRM variant to dash in, deliver its infantry squad, provide close-range fire support, and withdraw before heavier units can respond. The forward-firing arc limits the weapon's utility in running engagements but suits the hit-and-run insertion role.
text.deployment: The SRM hover APC fills a light cavalry role in many garrison and militia formations, combining troop delivery with modest anti-armor capability. Commands stationed in areas with significant light vehicle threats favor this variant over the base model, as the SRM-2 provides a meaningful deterrent against hostile scout vehicles and light tanks that might otherwise engage the transport with impunity.

text.capabilities:
The hover APC is the fastest of the three standard configurations, its air-cushion drive propelling the ten-ton vehicle to a maximum speed of over one hundred sixty kilometers per hour. This exceptional speed makes it ideal for rapid insertions and extractions across open terrain, though the hovercraft requires relatively flat ground to operate effectively. Two turret-mounted machine guns provide anti-infantry defense, while one ton of infantry carrying capacity accommodates a single squad of foot infantry.

The hover configuration carries twenty-four points of standard armor, the lightest protection of the three designs, a necessary compromise to maintain its speed advantage. A LongCom communications system and OptiTrack Techniques targeting array handle battlefield coordination. The vehicle's petrochemical-burning internal combustion engine is simple to maintain and fuel, though it limits the carrier to conventional ammunition-based weapons.
text.deployment: The hover APC serves in virtually every military force across the Inner Sphere and Periphery, with particular prevalence in formations that value speed and rapid deployment capability. Mercenary commands favor the hover variant for its ability to extract infantry quickly from deteriorating situations, while planetary militias stationed on worlds with extensive flatlands and deserts rely on it as their primary personnel transport.

text.capabilities:
The LRM variant of the tracked APC eliminates the infantry compartment, turret, and machine gun to mount a forward-firing LRM-5 launcher with one ton of ammunition. This conversion completely removes the vehicle's troop-carrying capability, repurposing the robust tracked chassis as a light missile platform. Forty points of standard armor distributed evenly across all facings provide solid protection for a vehicle of its weight class.

Operating at the same maximum speed of approximately ninety-seven kilometers per hour, the tracked LRM variant offers better survivability than the hover LRM conversion thanks to its heavier armor. Garrison forces and militia commands favor this variant for providing indirect fire support from hull-down positions, where the tracked chassis can negotiate rough terrain to reach firing positions inaccessible to wheeled vehicles.
text.deployment: The tracked LRM conversion serves garrison and militia forces across the Inner Sphere, providing cheap indirect fire support from positions accessible only to tracked vehicles. The variant sees particularly heavy use in mountainous and forested regions where its ability to reach hull-down firing positions in rough terrain gives it a significant tactical advantage over wheeled or hover LRM platforms.

text.capabilities:
The machine gun variant of the tracked APC removes the infantry compartment to mount three turret-mounted machine guns with a full ton of ammunition. With no troop-carrying capacity, this conversion serves as a dedicated anti-infantry patrol vehicle, using the tracked chassis's all-terrain capability to pursue enemy infantry across rough ground. The turret provides three-hundred-sixty-degree coverage, allowing the vehicle to engage threats from any direction.

Forty points of standard armor give the tracked MG variant substantially better protection than the hover MG conversion, allowing it to operate in closer proximity to enemy forces. The tracked drive system's ability to negotiate broken terrain makes this variant particularly effective in urban and jungle environments where hover vehicles cannot operate and wheeled vehicles struggle.
text.deployment: The tracked MG variant serves primarily with garrison forces and planetary militias for patrol and anti-infantry operations in rough terrain. Its combination of all-terrain mobility and concentrated machine gun fire makes it effective for operations in environments where hover and wheeled vehicles cannot operate, including dense urban areas, jungles, and mountainous regions.

text.capabilities:
The SRM variant of the tracked APC replaces the turret and machine gun with a forward-firing SRM-2 launcher while retaining one ton of infantry carrying capacity for a single squad. This configuration provides the transport with modest close-range anti-armor capability, allowing it to engage light vehicles and exposed BattleMech components while still fulfilling its primary troop delivery mission. One ton of SRM ammunition provides adequate endurance.

With forty points of standard armor evenly distributed and the tracked drive system's reliable all-terrain mobility, the SRM variant is better suited to close-range engagements than its hover counterpart. The tracked chassis's ability to use terrain for cover and approach from unexpected directions compensates for the forward-only firing arc of the SRM launcher.
text.deployment: The tracked SRM variant fills a light escort role in many infantry-heavy formations, providing close-range fire support while delivering a squad to the battle line. The tracked chassis's ability to follow infantry across rough terrain makes it particularly valuable as a fire support element that can remain with dismounted troops after delivery, unlike faster hover variants that typically withdraw immediately.

text.capabilities:
The tracked APC is the most robust of the three standard configurations, its tracked drive system providing reliable cross-country mobility across virtually any terrain type. The ten-ton vehicle reaches a maximum speed of approximately ninety-seven kilometers per hour -- slower than the hover variant but adequate for combined-arms operations alongside heavier vehicles. A single turret-mounted machine gun provides anti-infantry defense, while one ton of infantry carrying capacity accommodates a single squad of foot infantry.

The tracked configuration carries forty points of standard armor, substantially more protection than either the hover or wheeled versions, making it the most survivable of the three designs. This additional armor, concentrated on the front and flanks, allows the tracked APC to absorb incidental fire during combat insertions that would cripple its lighter counterparts. A LongCom communications system and OptiTrack Techniques targeting array handle battlefield coordination.
text.deployment: The tracked APC is the most widely fielded variant of the standard APC family, prized for its all-terrain capability and robust armor protection. Every major House military maintains large stocks of tracked APCs for infantry transport duties, and the design dominates in formations operating in rough, forested, or mountainous terrain where hover vehicles cannot function and wheeled vehicles are unreliable.

text.capabilities:
The LRM variant of the wheeled APC eliminates the infantry compartment, turret, and machine guns to mount a forward-firing LRM-5 launcher with one ton of ammunition. This conversion completely removes the vehicle's troop-carrying capability, creating a light missile platform with forty points of standard armor -- better protected than the hover LRM variant though matching the tracked conversion.

The wheeled LRM variant operates at approximately ninety-seven kilometers per hour on improved surfaces, where it can rapidly reposition between firing positions using established road networks. Garrison commands stationed in developed areas particularly favor this conversion, as the wheeled chassis provides adequate mobility for defensive operations while the armor improves crew survivability against counterbattery fire.
text.deployment: The wheeled LRM conversion serves garrison forces defending urban areas and industrial complexes, where road networks support rapid repositioning between firing positions. The variant's heavier armor compared to the hover LRM variant improves crew survivability in defensive operations where counterbattery fire is expected.

text.capabilities:
The machine gun variant of the wheeled APC removes the infantry compartment to mount four turret-mounted machine guns -- the heaviest machine gun battery of any standard APC variant -- with a full ton of ammunition. With no troop-carrying capacity, this conversion serves as a dedicated anti-infantry and riot-control platform, its four machine guns delivering devastating anti-personnel firepower from the turret's full traverse arc.

Forty-eight points of standard armor make the wheeled MG variant the most heavily protected of all standard APC configurations, allowing it to operate confidently against infantry armed with small arms and light anti-vehicle weapons. The wheeled drive system suits the urban and industrial environments where anti-infantry operations most commonly occur, and many planetary security forces use this variant as their primary patrol vehicle.
text.deployment: The wheeled MG variant is a common sight among planetary security forces and law enforcement organizations, where its combination of heavy armor and maximum machine gun firepower serves the riot-control and urban patrol role. Many worlds use this variant as their primary internal security vehicle, and its distinctive four-gun turret silhouette is recognized across the Inner Sphere.

text.capabilities:
The SRM variant of the wheeled APC replaces the standard turret armament with a turret-mounted SRM-2 launcher while retaining one ton of infantry carrying capacity for a single squad. The turret mounting gives the SRM launcher three-hundred-sixty-degree traverse, a significant advantage over the forward-firing SRM installations on the hover and tracked SRM variants. One ton of SRM ammunition provides adequate endurance for most operations.

With forty-eight points of standard armor -- the heaviest protection available on any standard APC variant -- and the SRM launcher's ability to engage targets from any direction, the wheeled SRM variant is the most combat-capable transport configuration in the standard APC family. The wheeled drive system's dependence on improved surfaces limits its operational flexibility compared to the tracked variant, but in urban and garrison environments it offers an effective combination of transport and fire support.
text.deployment: The wheeled SRM variant serves garrison and militia forces in urban environments, where its turret-mounted SRM launcher provides three-hundred-sixty-degree anti-armor coverage from a heavily armored platform. The turret mounting distinguishes it from the hover and tracked SRM variants, which carry their launchers in fixed forward mounts, giving the wheeled version superior tactical flexibility in the close-quarters engagements common in urban warfare.

text.capabilities:
The wheeled APC offers the best armor protection of the three standard configurations, its forty-eight points of standard armor providing a notable survivability advantage over the hover and tracked designs. The ten-ton vehicle reaches a maximum speed of approximately ninety-seven kilometers per hour on improved surfaces, where its wheeled drive system operates most efficiently. Two turret-mounted machine guns provide anti-infantry defense, while one ton of infantry carrying capacity accommodates a single squad of foot infantry.

The wheeled configuration excels in urban, industrial, and developed environments where road networks support rapid transit between positions. While less capable than tracked vehicles in rough terrain and unable to match the hover variant's speed across open ground, the wheeled APC's combination of heavier armor and reliable road performance makes it the preferred transport for garrison and urban operations. A LongCom communications system and OptiTrack Techniques targeting array handle battlefield coordination.
text.deployment: The wheeled APC sees its heaviest deployment in urban, industrial, and garrison environments where established road networks support its superior road mobility. The Lyran Commonwealth fields particularly large numbers of wheeled APCs along its extensive road networks, while planetary garrison forces across the Inner Sphere favor the design for its heavier armor protection in environments where the wheeled drive system's terrain limitations are less relevant.

text.overview: The Arrow IV Assault Vehicle is an eighty-ton tracked artillery platform developed by Majesty Metals and Manufacturing on Canopus IV and introduced in 3089. Conceived as a direct evolution of the Demolisher Arrow IV tank, the design sacrifices one of the Demolisher's two missile launchers to carry substantially heavier armor and a dedicated anti-missile suite, correcting a critical vulnerability in the original platform. Where the Demolisher proved susceptible to counterattack once enemy forces identified and closed with the artillery line, the AAV is engineered to absorb direct fire and continue its mission. Majesty Metals brought the design to market by capitalizing on the Magistracy Armed Forces' demonstrated appetite for Arrow IV artillery and the broader New Magistracy emphasis on indirect fire capability. Since its introduction, the AAV has established itself as one of the most durable heavy artillery vehicles available, spreading from its Canopian origins into service across the Inner Sphere.
text.capabilities:
The Arrow IV Assault Vehicle mounts a single Luxor I Arrow IV Artillery System as its primary weapon, trading the Demolisher's second launcher for a far more survivable combat profile. StarSlab/7 Heavy Ferro-Fibrous plating covers the hull, providing substantially heavier protection than the Demolisher and giving crews meaningful resistance against the direct fire most likely to target an exposed artillery position. CASE compartmentalization protects the main chassis from secondary explosions should the turret ammunition ignite. A GM 240 fusion engine provides power, delivering a cruising speed of 32 kilometers per hour adequate for repositioning within an engagement zone.

Two Blankenburg Medium Variable-Speed Pulse Lasers are mounted independently in the turret, allowing the AAV to engage closing infantry and light vehicles without interrupting Arrow IV bombardment cycles. A pair of LFN Lindblad Shotgun Anti-Missile Systems on the hull provides a meaningful defensive layer against incoming missiles, the attack profile most commonly used to suppress exposed artillery. The VSP lasers' independent turret mounting is a particular strength, letting crews track fast-moving threats without repositioning the hull and breaking firing solutions for the Arrow IV system.

The launch racks are designed with full modularity in mind: all ammunition is stored within the rack assembly itself rather than in the main hull, and the AAV's chassis is reinforced to tow its own ammunition trailers in a configuration reminiscent of older Long Tom land train concepts. Spent racks can be removed and replaced with fresh trailers directly on the battlefield, dramatically reducing reload time compared to conventional artillery vehicles. This logistical flexibility makes the AAV an attractive option for commands operating extended fire missions in contested areas.
text.deployment: The Arrow IV Assault Vehicle serves primarily within Magistracy Armed Forces artillery battalions, where its combination of firepower, survivability, and logistical flexibility has made it the preferred heavy Arrow IV platform over the older Demolisher type. The design can be found across the Free Worlds, with Brooks Incorporated's Andurien production line supplying units throughout that region since 3101. The type has spread to Taurian Concordat forces and mercenary commands operating across the Inner Sphere, and Lyran units along the Jade Falcon border have adopted the AAV for its ability to withstand the aggressive counterattacks that Clan forces mount against identified artillery positions.
text.battleHistory:
During Naomi Centralla's campaign to expel the Thirty-fourth Word of Blake Militia from Canopus IV, the Magistracy Armed Forces demonstrated the decisive potential of coordinated Arrow IV artillery. Demolisher tanks armed with Arrow IV systems served with the Red Lancers, using sustained barrage fire to herd Word of Blake formations into killing grounds and deny them freedom of maneuver. The battle convinced MAF High Command that Arrow IV artillery was a force multiplier worth pursuing at scale, and the Magistracy subsequently acquired large quantities of Capellan Arrow IV Demolishers to fill the gap while domestic production expanded.

The Demolisher carried a recognized operational weakness, however: its relatively light armor left crews vulnerable once enemy forces closed to neutralize the artillery threat. When counterattacking units reached the artillery line, Demolisher crews had limited options. Majesty Metals and Manufacturing recognized this gap and in 3089 released the Arrow IV Assault Vehicle. By accepting one fewer Arrow IV launcher, the AAV could carry protection far exceeding that of the Demolisher, transforming a vulnerable fire support vehicle into an artillery tank capable of surviving sustained direct engagement with its attackers. The New Magistracy's focus on Arrow IV artillery capability made the design a natural investment, and the MAF became the AAV's first and most committed customer.

Demand quickly outpaced Majesty Metals' production capacity at Canopus IV, and in 3101 the company licensed manufacturing rights to Brooks Incorporated at Andurien, extending the AAV's industrial base into Free Worlds League space. The design's combat reputation was cemented during the 3145 campaign on Almach, where Red Lancer AAVs withstood repeated attacks by a company of Davion Fulcrum hovertanks. The Fulcrums had been dispatched to silence the Arrow IV barrage suppressing the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry's withdrawal, expecting to face the lighter Demolisher type. Instead they found vehicles capable of absorbing their fire while the independently turreted lasers and anti-missile systems stripped away the Fulcrums' advantages. The uninterrupted bombardment kept the Armored Cavalry from disengaging as the Red Lancers' BattleMechs finished the engagement. The AAV's performance at Almach validated the design philosophy Majesty Metals had pursued since 3089, and demand continued to grow throughout the Dark Age period.

text.overview: The Arrow IV Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle mounting two Arrow IV artillery systems on the standard weapons carrier chassis. Produced by the Quikscell Company for the Draconis Combine beginning in 3058, the design provides cheap artillery fire support using the proven carrier platform. The Arrow IV system's homing capability gives the vehicle precision strike potential far exceeding conventional missile carriers.
text.capabilities:
The Arrow IV Carrier mounts two forward-firing Arrow IV artillery launchers, providing both conventional area-effect bombardment and precision homing strikes when paired with TAG designators. An InterComBust 180 internal combustion engine maintains the standard fifty-four kilometer per hour top speed. Simple Armor Plate Standard provides the same minimal forty-eight point armor protection as other base-model carriers.

A Communicator system and FireScan with IndirecTrack targeting handle coordination and fire direction. The Arrow IV system's indirect fire capability allows the carrier to operate from defilade positions well behind the front line, reducing exposure to the direct combat that proves fatal to thinly armored carrier platforms.
text.deployment: The Arrow IV Carrier was produced by Quikscell for the Draconis Combine beginning in 3058, with production at Ares, Kalidasa, Layover, and Oliver. The DCMS integrated the design into combined-arms formations requiring organic artillery support at the company level.
text.battleHistory:
The Arrow IV Carrier was developed for the Draconis Combine beginning in 3058, utilizing the proven Quikscell carrier chassis to mount Arrow IV artillery systems. The design appeared in Field Manual: Draconis Combine, reflecting DCMS doctrine favoring artillery integration at the company level. Quikscell produced the vehicle at four plants: Ares, Kalidasa, Layover, and Oliver.

The Arrow IV system's ability to fire both standard and homing munitions provides the carrier with precision strike capability far beyond conventional missile platforms. The design proved adaptable enough that other Quikscell carrier facilities could produce it with minimal retooling, leveraging the shared chassis and engine configuration.

text.overview: The Asshur Artillery Spotter is a dedicated fire support coordination platform developed from the original Asshur Fast Reconnaissance Vehicle. When the lighter Shamash entered service and made the Asshur's reconnaissance mission redundant, Clan Blood Spirit technicians devised a modification that replaced the hull-mounted machine guns with a Target Acquisition Gear system, converting the vehicle into a capable artillery coordination asset. Entering service in 2893, the Artillery Spotter retained all the speed and mobility of the base chassis while gaining a specialization that gave it a permanent battlefield role long after its original function was superseded. The modification proved so successful that it was adopted across multiple Clans and became the dominant Asshur production standard, eventually reaching both the Clan Homeworlds and the Inner Sphere during Clan operations in the thirty-first century.
text.capabilities:
The Artillery Spotter's primary contribution to a combined arms formation is not its direct weapons fire but its Target Acquisition Gear system, which designates targets for Arrow IV artillery missiles and similar guided munitions. The ICD Type 4 TAG unit is mounted fixed-forward in the vehicle rather than in the turret. Early attempts to mount the system in the turret created interference with the traverse mechanism, degrading both TAG performance and the vehicle's ability to defend itself. Relocating the designator to a fixed hull mount resolved the interference problem at the cost of a limited designation arc, requiring the crew to orient the vehicle toward the target rather than relying on turret traverse. The Asshur's speed and agility largely compensate for this constraint.

Direct defensive armament consists of two Series 2b extended-range medium lasers and a Pattern J6 Streak-6 SRM launcher, all turret-mounted. The Streak system is particularly effective for a platform of this type, as its guaranteed-hit characteristic ensures that the limited supply of fifteen missile volleys is not wasted on ineffective shots. The extended-range lasers allow accurate fire out to 450 meters, enabling the crew to engage threats while maintaining the standoff distance needed for effective target designation.

Ferro-fibrous armor provides moderate protection suited to a platform intended to operate behind the forward edge of battle. The Consolidated electronics suite is carried over from the base chassis, prioritizing reliable communications (essential for effective spotting coordination) over enhanced targeting performance.
text.deployment: The Artillery Spotter serves as a combined arms coordination asset across Clan formations equipped with Arrow IV artillery support. Clan Blood Spirit, Burrock, Coyote, Ice Hellion, Snow Raven, and later Ghost Bear and Sea Fox forces all operated the variant, with production maintained at facilities on Albion, Tamaron, Hector, Lum, York, and Trondheim across different eras. Ghost Bear and Steel Viper toumans deployed the variant in the Inner Sphere during the Clan Invasion, with Steel Viper forces particularly employing Asshurs on Graus in 3054 to coordinate Arrow IV strikes against mercenary raiders to lethal effect. Ghost Bear production at the Trondheim facility extended availability into the former Free Rasalhague Republic, while Homeworld facilities continued supplying Clans remaining in Clan space through the Civil War and beyond.
text.battleHistory:
The Artillery Spotter variant emerged as a practical solution to a specific problem in Clan Blood Spirit's force structure. When Blood Spirit scientists completed the Shamash reconnaissance vehicle, its lighter design and equivalent sensor capability made the original Asshur Fast Reconnaissance Vehicle redundant in the scouting role. Rather than retire serviceable hulls (a course that would have wasted significant resources during the challenging Homeworld period) Blood Spirit technicians identified the platform's remaining strengths and reoriented it toward a complementary mission.

The central challenge was integrating a Target Acquisition Gear system into a hull not designed around it. Early attempts to mount the TAG in the turret alongside the existing laser armament created problems with the traverse mechanism, with the system's alignment requirements conflicting with free rotation. The solution was a fixed-forward hull mount, accepting a limited designation arc in exchange for reliable operation. Field experience quickly demonstrated that the Asshur's speed compensated effectively for this limitation, as crews could reorient the vehicle to bring the TAG to bear without meaningful exposure to return fire.

The Artillery Spotter entered service in 2893, with York's production facilities among the first to incorporate the modification. The conversion proved so capable in combined arms operations (particularly coordinating Arrow IV artillery assets) that other Clans with Asshur production access adopted the configuration as well. Albion, Tamaron, Hector, and Lum facilities all transitioned to Artillery Spotter production over subsequent decades, making it the dominant variant across the Homeworld production network. The base reconnaissance configuration was effectively supplanted in new production, though existing hulls continued in secondary service.

During the Clan Invasion, the Artillery Spotter accompanied Clan forces into the Inner Sphere. Ghost Bear and Steel Viper elements deployed the vehicle in several engagements, most especially during the 3054 raid on Graus, where Steel Viper forces encountered the mercenary company Armstrong's Archers. Operating under contract to the Federated Commonwealth, the Archers staged a raid against the Thirty-eighth Phalanx 250 kilometers north of New Paris. The Inner Sphere commander, unaware that one of the vehicles in the Star's formation was an Asshur spotter, concentrated on engaging the two BattleMechs and disregarded the vehicle elements as a lower priority threat. The Asshur's crew used this oversight to designate targets for Arrow IV artillery missiles continuously throughout the engagement, guiding strikes from a pair of tanks located several kilometers from the battlefield. No mercenaries survived.

Ghost Bear established a new production line at the New York Vehicle Y2 Facility on Trondheim following the Clan's occupation of the former Free Rasalhague Republic, bringing Asshur Artillery Spotter production into the Inner Sphere proper. This facility operated under successive Clan Sea Fox stewardship from the later Civil War period onward, sustaining production into the Dark Age and ilClan eras. The Homeworld facilities continued operating under their respective Clan owners, with Hector passing through Ice Hellion, Goliath Scorpion, and Cloud Cobra hands across the Jihad and Dark Age periods.
