Both weapons are oriented toward discouraging pursuit rather than engaging in sustained combat, and the designers recognized early that a Beagle crew attempting to fight rather than scout was a crew doing the wrong job. The Essex 88 communications system ensures reliable coordination with the larger formation the vehicle supports, making the Beagle as much a communications node as a sensor platform.
text.deployment: The TAG variant is designed to serve as a spotter for non-C3i units, pairing its retained Beagle Active Probe with targeting acquisition gear to designate enemies for semi-guided munitions and orbital fire support. A Guardian ECM suite keeps the vehicle off enemy sensors while it stalks formations at range, and the XL engine matches the C3i variant's 226 kilometers per hour top speed. The TAG variant retains the standard Beagle's laser weapons, giving crews a measure of self-defense that the C3i model lacks. Word of Blake crews preferred to deploy these vehicles in pairs, ranging the battlefield to call in LRM barrages and, in some cases, support from orbiting WarShips against Davion defenders. After the Jihad the Republic of the Sphere continued production and the Capellan Confederation maintained the line into the ilClan period.

The standard Behemoth Heavy Tank is distributed across virtually every Inner Sphere military, with the heaviest concentrations remaining in Federated Suns, Capellan, and Draconis Combine armored formations. It performs best in prepared defensive positions, urban environments, and chokepoint defense where its limited mobility is less exploitable. Commanders typically pair Behemoths with faster screening elements to compensate for their inability to reposition quickly under fire.

The Armor variant trades a portion of the standard Behemoth's secondary weapons for additional hull protection, making it favored by garrison commanders anticipating sustained siege conditions rather than fluid engagements. The added survivability comes at the cost of close-range anti-infantry capability, making it more reliant on support units when facing dismounted infantry threats.

General Motors' Davion variant, introduced in the 3080s as part of the Federated Suns' post-Jihad rearmament program, equips AFFS heavy armor formations with a significantly upgraded capability. The Gauss rifle battery and ferro-fibrous armor with CASE provide a threat profile well above the standard Behemoth, and the variant has been selectively exported to allied forces during the Dark Age. Production at Salem has been continuous since its introduction.

The Flamer variant substitutes flamers for the Behemoth's short-range missile racks, converting the vehicle into a dedicated anti-infantry and anti-light-vehicle platform. It appears in garrison and pacification roles across all Inner Sphere factions, and is particularly valued in dense urban and forested terrain where conventional armor finds infantry difficult to suppress. The conversion is a common field modification requiring minimal specialized equipment.

New Samarkand Metals' most advanced Behemoth configuration mounts Clan-grade Streak launchers and Ultra-class autocannons alongside a targeting computer, placing it firmly in the company of dedicated tank destroyers. Fielded exclusively by DCMS elite armored formations from the mid-Dark Age onward, the Kurita Upgrade variant has seen action in the border skirmishes and major campaigns that have defined the Dark Age period.

New Samarkand Metals' Kurita variant serves as the backbone of Draconis Combine heavy armor formations from the early thirty-first century onward. Its fusion engine and updated weapon battery make it considerably more capable than the original ICE-powered design, and the variant has proven effective in the assault and breakthrough roles that Combine armored doctrine emphasizes. Concentrations remain heaviest in formations stationed along the Federated Suns border.

Produced at Aldis Industries' Betelgeuse facility as a stopgap measure when XL engine shortages disrupted Behemoth II output, the Liao variant grafts upgraded weaponry onto a standard Behemoth chassis to maintain production continuity. Deployed by Capellan forces during the Dark Age, it provides a capable if unconventional fire support asset that benefits from the logistical simplicity of the ICE powerplant in the resource-constrained environments common to that era.

The Refit variant appeared in the 3060s as a straightforward upgrade option, replacing the original MaxiCannon battery with LB 10-X autocannons and adding CASE protection. It was produced at factory level by Aldis Industries at both Betelgeuse and Terra, and also executed as a common field modification across Inner Sphere forces. The ammunition flexibility of the LB 10-X autocannon was considered a significant operational advantage over the original fixed-ammunition design, and the CASE installation meaningfully improved crew survivability against ammunition-cook-off events.

The Behemoth II serves as a heavy breakthrough element and mobile defensive anchor for Capellan and Republic armored formations. Its combination of speed and firepower allows it to hold ground against numerically superior opposition while retaining enough mobility to reposition under threat, addressing the original Behemoth's most significant tactical limitation. Commanders prize it for defensive operations but remain attentive to its XL engine vulnerability and logistical demands relative to simpler designs.

The Support variant exchanges the Gauss rifle for an ER large laser and mixes in LRM and Streak SRM fire control, shifting the Behemoth II into a more flexible fire support role at the expense of maximum single-target penetration. It serves alongside standard Behemoth IIs in mixed platoons, providing sustained-fire capability and extended-range engagement options that complement the primary variant's precision Gauss battery.

The base Bellona was distributed among Hell's Horses frontline Clusters engaged against Clan Wolf and Clan Ice Hellion during the Jihad, primarily in the fighting across the Horses' contested occupation corridor. Given severe supply constraints imposed by the Homeworld logistics chain, individual Stars and Points were seeded into existing vehicle Stars rather than forming dedicated Bellona formations. As Csesztreg production ramped up during the Dark Age, Hell's Horses garrison and frontline Clusters throughout the occupation zones received the Bellona in larger numbers, and it has become the standard fast cavalry vehicle in Hell's Horses toumans across the Inner Sphere holdings.

The laser variant addresses the Bellona's principal vulnerability to ammunition shortages by replacing the autocannon with an extended-range large laser, providing a reliable primary weapon regardless of supply conditions during extended operations. An LRM-10 battery supplements the laser, maintaining indirect fire capability for harassment missions. While the retained ammunition dependency of the missile launcher is a partial measure, the laser gives Hell's Horses cavalry commanders the long-range harassment and engagement reach they prize most. The variant was planned during the Jihad but reached deployment after production moved to Csesztreg, and it serves alongside the base model in frontline Clusters where supply lines remain uncertain.

The XL variant upgrades the Bellona with an extralight engine, reducing the powerplant's mass and freeing tonnage for additional systems while preserving the hover chassis's high-speed performance. Introduced in the early Dark Age as Csesztreg production matured, it represents the current-generation production standard for Hell's Horses cavalry formations and is produced exclusively at Csesztreg Industriplex Beta. The XL variant has replaced earlier models in frontline units as attrition and resupply cycles allow, and it serves throughout Hell's Horses toumans in the ilClan era as the preferred fast-strike platform.

The standard Blizzard performs straightforward infantry transport duties, operating in rapid-insertion or reconnaissance support roles where speed takes priority over protection. Its low acquisition and maintenance cost makes it accessible to militia forces, second-tier mercenary commands, and planetary defense units that cannot afford heavier transports. The vehicle functions best when paired with heavier combat assets that can absorb direct fire while the Blizzard completes its delivery runs. On worlds with open terrain, wetlands, or coastal geography, its hovercraft propulsion allows it to cross terrain that would stop wheeled or tracked vehicles entirely. Most operators hold it back from direct engagement, releasing it only once infantry support has suppressed the nearest anti-vehicle threat.

The Black Blizzard strips the infantry bay entirely and reconfigures the vehicle as a dedicated escort platform. Ferro-fibrous armor replaces the standard protection, improving survivability significantly over the transport variants. Paired SRM-4 launchers and machine guns in the turret, combined with a Guardian ECM suite, give the escort meaningful offensive capability and electronic protection for the formations it accompanies. The Black Blizzard is intended to operate alongside standard Blizzards, screening their approach and withdrawal against light combat vehicles and infantry threats. It is not suited for prolonged independent operations, but in its assigned escort role it substantially improves the survivability of the transport lance as a whole. The Word of Blake's Epsilon Eridani militia was the most prominent early operator, and the variant spread to other independent world forces through the post-Jihad period.

The SRM variant substitutes a pair of SRM-2 launchers for the base model's long-range missile system, sacrificing standoff range for improved performance at close quarters. Introduced in 3062, this modification was developed for the urban and suburban environments of the Chaos March, where open sightlines are rare and the base model's range advantage seldom materializes. The SRM variant operates interchangeably with standard Blizzards in mixed transport lances, carrying the same infantry payload under identical crew and logistical requirements. It is particularly common among Chaos March militias and mercenary units operating in dense terrain, and it continues to see service in successor state reserve formations that inherited vehicles from the Republic period.

The A configuration transforms the Bolla into a long-range precision platform. A light Gauss rifle enhanced by a targeting computer provides exceptional accuracy at extended ranges, while an anti-missile system protects against incoming missile fire. A TAG designator extends the configuration’s utility beyond direct fire to target designation for supporting assets. The A’s emphasis on stand-off precision makes it well-suited to special operations missions where the stealth approach allows the vehicle to acquire and engage high-value targets before defenders can locate the firing position.

The B configuration serves a command-and-coordination role within Republic special operations. A C²-master computer allows the vehicle to function as a command unit for an entire lance of C³-slaved vehicles, while the fixed C³ slave allows it to simultaneously integrate into a full C³ company network. Paired multi-missile launchers and Magshot Gauss rifles provide direct-fire capability, but the B’s primary value lies in its ability to distribute superior targeting data across an entire special operations element, multiplying the effectiveness of units it coordinates.

The C configuration is a well-rounded close-action variant combining a light autocannon loaded with precision ammunition, paired Streak SRM launchers for reliable short-range engagement, and a secondary machine gun for anti-infantry work. A TAG system maintains combined-arms coordination capability. The C’s balanced armament mix makes it the most adaptable RotS Bolla configuration for direct engagements where target types cannot be predicted in advance, and it is reportedly among the more commonly assigned variants in special forces units expecting contact during insertion operations.

The D configuration represents an updated weapons loadout introduced in the Dark Ages era, developed by Maxwell-Pulaski Motors for continued Republic special forces deployment. Details of the D’s specific armament remain limited in open-source reporting, consistent with the Republic’s broader practice of maintaining operational security around new Bolla configurations. As with other RotS variants, the D is assigned exclusively to Republic special forces elements and successor formations operating within the established doctrine framework for covert battle armor delivery.

The Prime configuration serves as the standard Republic Bolla loadout and reference platform for most special forces training and doctrine. A second machine gun bolsters anti-infantry coverage, a rotary autocannon provides sustained fire across engagement ranges, and paired multi-missile launchers extend the vehicle’s ability to threaten targets at varied distances. A TAG designator allows the Prime to coordinate with artillery and air-delivered munitions, extending its utility in combined-arms special operations. Deployed exclusively within Republic special forces, the Prime’s existence and capabilities remain classified outside a narrow circle of authorized personnel.

The Comminus was the least commonly encountered of the four Blakist Bolla configurations during the Jihad, though it was sufficiently documented that coalition intelligence services tracked it separately from the more prevalent Invictus. Like the other Blakist variants, the Comminus retains the larger infantry bay and C³i integration that characterized the original design. Surviving examples in post-Jihad inventories are concentrated primarily in Republic Armed Forces stocks, where the RAF’s larger consolidated collection of all original Bolla configurations supports broader technical understanding of the design family.

text.capabilities:
The Bolla’s defining capability is its stealth armor system, which substantially degrades enemy targeting effectiveness at medium and long range and allows the vehicle to advance across open terrain with a survivability impossible for conventional wheeled transports. The single fixed machine gun is a deliberately minimal armament reflecting the vehicle’s primary role as a delivery platform rather than a direct combatant. The real striking power lies in the battle armor squad carried in the infantry bay, sized in original Blakist production for a full six-trooper Level I in accordance with Word of Blake organizational doctrine. A C³i system integrates the crew and embarked infantry into a unified targeting network with any linked C³i units nearby, allowing coordinated strikes with a precision difficult for conventional forces to match.

The turret accommodates variant-specific weapon loads that allow the Bolla to adapt to different tactical roles. The chassis design provides pod space for configurations ranging from close assault to long-range precision engagement, giving unit commanders mission flexibility that fixed-load vehicles cannot offer. The wheeled drive and XL fusion plant deliver a road speed that makes the vehicle difficult to overtake in pursuit scenarios, while the stealth system remains the primary defensive capability against detection during approach. The XL plant is a vulnerability, as battle damage to the engine compartment risks catastrophic power loss, a trade-off the designers accepted to preserve payload capacity for the infantry bay and weapons systems.
text.deployment: The Infernus appeared during the Jihad as one of the less frequently documented Bolla configurations, noted in coalition after-action reports from engagements around Terra. Operating alongside the more common Invictus, the Infernus fulfilled mission profiles suited to its specific weapon and systems fit within Blakist special operations doctrine. Captured examples entered coalition and successor-state inventories through post-Jihad battlefield recovery, where they contribute to the broader pool of former Blakist covert-operations technology being maintained by interested parties across the Inner Sphere.

The Invictus served as the primary Blakist Bolla configuration and was the most frequently encountered variant among coalition forces during the Jihad. Assigned to specialized infiltration units across Blakist-controlled space, the Invictus handled the standard mission profile of stealth approach and battle armor insertion for strike operations. Following the Jihad, captured examples appear in small numbers across multiple Inner Sphere factions distributed through post-conflict salvage operations. The Lyran Commonwealth, Federated Suns, Draconis Combine, and former Free Worlds states each maintain a handful, though maintenance demands associated with the stealth system limit operational availability outside dedicated technical support arrangements.

The standard Browning serves as the primary command vehicle for regiment and smaller combined-arms formations. Republic forces fielded the greatest numbers, followed by the Federated Suns after Julian Davion's acquisition of former Republic equipment. The AFFS has deployed Brownings in campaigns across the Capellan March and Draconis March, where their ECM and communications capabilities proved invaluable for coordinating multi-regiment operations from forward positions.

The Browning Half-Track is a limited-production variant that replaces the standard wheeled suspension with a half-tracked drivetrain, offering improved mobility on rough terrain at the cost of top speed. Republic forces used this model on worlds where road infrastructure was poor or nonexistent, and the AFFS adopted several during the expansion of former Republic territories. Half-Tracks are rare enough that spotting one usually indicates a formation with Republic heritage or direct access to Mitchell Vehicles' production line.

The standard Brutus is the most widely distributed of the production variants, serving with Federated Suns Regimental Combat Teams, Capellan Confederation second-line formations, and a range of Chaos March militia commands. Its balanced weapon mix makes it a dependable general-purpose fire support vehicle capable of engaging at any range. Kressly WarWorks' steady production kept supply high enough to spread the design across multiple successor state inventories following the Fourth Succession War.

Introduced during the Jihad, the HPPC Brutus replaces the standard energy weapons with a heavy particle projector cannon, generating significantly more damage per shot at the cost of sustained fire volume. The mass budget freed by the weapon change accommodates a C3 slave unit, enabling the tank to operate as a networked fire platform within coordinated formations. The variant is found primarily in Word of Blake and later Republic of the Sphere units that fielded C3-enabled combined-arms groups, where the heavy PPC's damage output is amplified further by shared targeting data.

text.overview: Built in the late 2990s at Kressly WarWorks' Epsilon Eridani facility, the Brutus Assault Tank was designed to give the Capellan Confederation's second-line forces an affordable heavy fire support platform capable of engaging targets at every range. Drawing on established industrial suppliers, Kressly built a practical if unspectacular vehicle that proved more capable in sustained combat than its early garrison assignments suggested. The Fourth Succession War expanded the Brutus's reach far beyond its Capellan origins, and subsequent political changes on Epsilon Eridani brought the design to Federated Commonwealth formations, Chaos March militias, and eventually the Word of Blake Protectorate. By the mid-thirty-first century, the Brutus had become one of the most broadly distributed heavy combat vehicles in the Inner Sphere, evidence of both its durability and the longevity of the Kressly production line.
text.deployment: The LRM variant replaces the standard energy weapons with a second long-range missile rack and expands ammunition capacity, increasing sustained missile output at the cost of independent energy firepower. Armor protection is modestly improved. The variant appeals to commanders who prioritize missile saturation in open terrain engagements and typically operates alongside lighter screening units that handle short-range threats. It is found primarily in Federated Commonwealth and successor Federated Suns units that favor missile-heavy combined-arms formations.

text.deployment: The second PPC variant replaces both the standard energy weapons and missile rack with a pair of Parti-Kill Heavy Cannons and adds additional armor protection. The heavier cannon armament delivers concentrated firepower at medium range, and the improved armor makes the variant more survivable than the standard Brutus. The variant is commonly deployed alongside Myrmidon medium tanks, where the complementary weapon mixes create effective combined-arms formations across Federated Suns and later Chaos March battlefields.

text.deployment: The PPC Brutus is a factory-built variant that reconfigures the standard weapon arrangement around particle projector cannon armament, trading the original missile dependency for clean energy firepower. The variant suits extended operations where ammunition resupply is unreliable and has found service across multiple operator factions seeking a lower-logistics alternative to the standard model. Its reliable energy-only armament simplifies maintenance in austere conditions and makes it a common choice for independent planetary defense commands operating without formal resupply chains.

The standard Bulldog fills a critical role as the Inner Sphere's most available and affordable medium tracked combat vehicle, deployed across planetary militias, garrison commands, and second-line conventional formations from the Periphery to the Clan border. The Draconis Combine and Capellan Confederation maintain the largest operational concentrations, with Proserpina and Ares output supplying conventional regiments throughout both states. The type's low cost and reparability make it attractive for any formation unable to sustain losses of premium equipment, and captured examples routinely return to service under opposing colors. Combined-arms formations use the standard Bulldog for screening, pursuit, and volume fire support, where its adequate firepower at moderate range complements heavier vehicles assigned to direct assault roles.

This field modification replaces the large laser with an Autocannon/2, extending the tank's effective engagement range and providing sustained harassment fire against dug-in positions. The refit emerged during the Succession Wars as units with reliable autocannon ammunition stocks sought to maximize the Bulldog's utility at ranges where energy weapons proved less effective. The modification has been independently developed across multiple factions that inherited or captured Bulldog stocks, and it remains common in units operating in logistics environments where autocannon resupply is more dependable than energy weapon maintenance support.

Introduced to Draconis Combine service following the Jihad, this variant replaces the original internal combustion powerplant with a fuel cell engine, reducing harmful emissions during operations in enclosed environments such as sealed industrial facilities and inhabited urban areas under environmental protection protocols. Combat performance matches the standard model in all respects. Production at Proserpina supplies DCMS conventional forces rebuilding their strength from Jihad-era losses, and the Cell variant has gradually displaced older ICE-powered hulks in Combine garrison units requiring cleaner operational profiles.

The Draconis Combine's most ambitious rework of the Bulldog chassis installs a significantly larger engine and a substantial quantity of hardened armor, producing a vehicle with protection well exceeding that of typical medium tanks in its weight class. A chemical laser provides primary armament, its ammunition dependency offset by the enhanced armor that allows the vehicle to operate at effective engagement ranges. Produced exclusively on Proserpina, the Chemical variant represents the Combine's effort to field a medium conventional vehicle capable of engaging ilClan-era threats that would have overwhelmed earlier Bulldog models.

The most significant modernization of the standard Bulldog, the ERLL variant upgrades the primary laser for extended-range performance, fits heavy ferro-fibrous armor with CASE for improved survivability, and adds an Artemis IV fire control system to enhance missile accuracy. A fuel cell engine replaces the original powerplant. Produced at both Proserpina and Ares, the ERLL serves as the baseline for further Draconis Combine and Capellan Confederation development and represents the standard production Bulldog for both states throughout the Republic and Dark Age eras.

A Capellan Confederation anti-aircraft and multi-role variant, the LB-X converts the primary weapon position to mount twin LB 5-X autocannons capable of firing both solid armor-piercing and cluster munitions. In the air defense role, cluster ammunition makes the variant an effective deterrent against VTOLs and conventional aerospace support. Against ground targets, solid shot provides credible anti-vehicle performance. Produced on Ares and deployed primarily with Capellan conventional forces, the LB-X is often encountered in mixed batteries protecting rear-area installations from aerial threat.

The LRM field modification converts the Bulldog into a fire support vehicle by replacing the short-range missile complement with a long-range missile system, providing indirect fire capability for units without access to dedicated artillery assets. First documented in use during the late Succession Wars, the refit is well suited to garrison formations protecting fixed positions or supporting attritional campaigns where sustained bombardment at standoff range is more valuable than close-range combat performance. The variant appears in service across virtually every faction that has operated large numbers of standard Bulldogs.

Optimized for operations against conventional infantry and lightly armored vehicles, this Capellan variant replaces the ERLL with a plasma rifle whose extreme heat and incendiary effects are particularly effective against targets with limited thermal protection. Capellan strategists developed the variant in response to the proliferation of conventional infantry threats within their operational territory during the Dark Age, where maintaining infantry suppression without committing heavy BattleMechs became a priority. Produced on Ares, the Plasma variant is most commonly encountered in Capellan interior operations where conventional ground forces represent the primary opposing threat.

The updated Bulwark has become the standard production variant for Free Worlds League heavy armor commands following its 3114 introduction, replacing earlier vehicles in units previously equipped with the Original variant. Priority allocation goes to front-line heavy armor formations assigned breakthrough and sustained defensive roles, where the combination of superior firepower and heavy protection delivers decisive results. The design has also drawn consistent mercenary interest, with several commands operating Bulwarks alongside conventional BattleMech forces in high-intensity contracts across the Inner Sphere.

The Original Bulwark, manufactured between 3087 and 3114, armed its crew with a first-generation heavy Gauss rifle in the main mount and a turret-mounted Gauss rifle as a secondary weapon, in place of the heavy particle cannon armament found on later production. It lacked the heavy ferro-fibrous armor of subsequent variants, relying on standard protection adequate for a vehicle of its class but inferior to what the 3114 update would provide. These vehicles served primarily in Free Worlds League defensive formations and were progressively withdrawn or cannibalized as the improved production run entered service. It is not unusual to encounter both Bulwark variants in the same unit, as the two are produced by the same company and share the same factory origin.

The Burke served throughout its operational life as a static defense platform, best employed in hull-down positions and fortified lines where its limited speed presented no tactical liability. SLDF heavy tank regiments deployed the Burke as their primary garrison asset, assigning it to command defensive zones while faster screening elements protected its flanks. In the aftermath of the Star League's collapse, Com Guard formations employed surviving Burkes in similar garrison roles, favoring the vehicle's long-range firepower for fixed defensive assignments. The Word of Blake used the type in comparable fashion, and Hell's Horses formations preserved it in heavy armor units. Commanders consistently pair the Burke with faster screening forces to compensate for its vulnerability to mobile opponents.

Developed during the Jihad by both the Word of Blake and ComStar, the HPPC variant replaced the Burke's three particle cannons with two Supernova heavy PPCs and substituted the LRM rack for a Holly Streak SRM-4 with two tons of ammunition. The most significant addition was a C³i unit, allowing the HPPC variant to share targeting data within larger networked formations and apply the Burke's heavy firepower as a coordinated element of combined-arms operations. Deployed exclusively in Word of Blake and ComStar garrison assignments during the Jihad, the variant extended the operational relevance of surviving Burke hulls by integrating them into the sophisticated command and control systems both organizations maintained.

Introduced in 2713 in response to persistent field complaints about the standard Burke's limited mobility, the Royal variant incorporated a VOX extralight engine providing a fifty-percent improvement in cruising speed. The LRM rack was removed in favor of two Streak SRM-2 launchers, and the weight savings allowed armor protection to increase to eight and a half tons of ferro-fibrous plate. A fleet-wide upgrade program was ordered in the years before the Amaris Coup, but production and supply constraints meant that only about half the active Burke fleet received the improvements before the campaign began. Royal variants became highly sought after in post-Succession War arsenals, particularly in Com Guard formations, where their improved mobility made them more tactically flexible than standard Burkes while retaining the formidable firepower that defined the family.

text.overview: The Burke II Superheavy Tank is a one-hundred-forty-ton experimental tracked vehicle designed by Leopard Armor on Terra during the Amaris Civil War. Amaris forces occupying Terra, impressed by the standard Burke's defensive capabilities, directed Leopard Armor to design and prototype a vehicle even more formidable than the original. The result outmassed even the Behemoth, the largest standard tank then in production. Only two prototypes were ever completed, both pressed directly into combat against SLDF forces during the recapture of Terra. The destruction of both prototypes and the production facilities in the same engagement ended any prospect of further development, leaving the Burke II as a single-incident footnote in Amaris Civil War history rather than a production design with lasting legacy.
text.capabilities:
The Burke II mounts four class-20 autocannons in its main turret, delivering firepower that doubles even the most heavily armed standard combat vehicles and is capable of reducing most BattleMech chassis to wreckage through sheer volume of fire. A pair of front-mounted LRM-5 launchers provides supplemental long-range engagement capability, though in practice the autocannons' overwhelming close-range firepower made the missiles secondary to the crew's tactical priorities. The prototypes' crews reportedly fired the launchers infrequently, preferring to hold position and wait for opponents to close into autocannon range.

A 280-rated fusion engine moves the superheavy hull at modest speed for a vehicle of its class. Ferro-fibrous armor distributed across the massive frame, with the heaviest concentration in the frontal arc and turret, provides substantial protection. The Burke II's fundamental tactical limitation mirrors its greatest strength: the four autocannons demand that opponents close to effective range, but the vehicle lacks the mobility to force that engagement against a determined enemy who chooses to maintain distance. The design carried notable quirks including Distracting capability, Prototype status, and Trailer Hitch and Rumble Seat fittings.
text.deployment: The Burke II existed only as two experimental prototypes and never entered organized deployment. Both vehicles were committed to a single defensive engagement near Munich during the SLDF's recapture of Terra, using terrain masking from airport infrastructure to offset their size and limited mobility. The engagement demonstrated the concept's viability as an ambush platform but ended with the destruction of both prototypes and the production facilities, foreclosing any further development or tactical evaluation. No deployment doctrine was developed for the type, and it left no successors.
text.battleHistory:
The Burke II's history is brief and concentrated in a single campaign. Rim Worlds forces occupying Terra had developed a deep appreciation for the Burke's defensive performance and directed Leopard Armor engineers to develop a larger and more powerful successor. Project Supervisor Mathias Gustasson began formal design work in August 2776, scaling the Burke concept to a superheavy platform and replacing the particle cannons with four class-20 autocannons. The design retained the aesthetic approach of the original Burke while dramatically increasing both its mass and firepower.

Only two frames were completed before operational necessity demanded their immediate deployment. Both prototypes were committed to the Amaris defense of Europe, operating from the tarmac of a decommissioned airport near Munich where port infrastructure provided concealment for vehicles of their extraordinary size. Using the facility's heavy walls to mask their movement, the crews ambushed SLDF armor columns crossing open ground and reportedly performed well in the role, demonstrating that the concept of a superheavy vehicle armed with multiple class-20 autocannons had practical merit.

The defense ultimately failed when one prototype exhausted its ammunition supply and an SLDF 'Mech lance arrived to overwhelm it. The second prototype was destroyed in the engagement that followed. When SLDF forces secured the Leopard Armor facilities, the production molds and tooling needed to build additional Burke IIs were destroyed along with surviving documentation. No attempt to recreate the design has been made in the centuries since, and the vehicle remains a historical curiosity rather than an ancestor to any subsequent production line.

text.overview: The Buzzard Hover Tank entered production in 3076 as Quikscell Company's response to client demand for a fire support variant of the Falcon platform better suited to standoff engagements than close-range combat. Introduced during the late Jihad at the Richvale facility, the Buzzard trades the Falcon's exceptional top speed for a heavier armament suite capable of reaching targets at longer ranges. An alternative powerplant design provides the energy profile that makes the heavier weapons load practical while keeping costs within reach of cash-strapped buyers. Like all Quikscell products, the Buzzard reached isolated planetary governments and militia forces as a partially assembled kit through the same distribution network that sustained the Hawk and Falcon through decades of production. The design filled a genuine gap for forces needing standoff fire support at hovercraft prices rather than BattleMech costs.
text.capabilities:
The Buzzard's fuel cell powerplant replaces the Falcon's ICE engine, freeing sufficient mass for a particle cannon and multi-missile launchers. This weapon combination extends the vehicle's effective engagement range well beyond the Falcon's short-range missile loadout. The particle cannon delivers precision direct fire against armored targets at extended ranges, while the multi-missile launchers accept both short and long-range ammunition, allowing crews to adapt their fire to the tactical situation. Trading top speed for this heavier armament makes the Buzzard more dependent on terrain selection and pre-positioning than the Falcon, as reduced hover speed limits the crew's ability to disengage rapidly from unfavorable engagements.

ProtecTech Light armor matches the Falcon's protection standard, keeping the Buzzard within the light combat vehicle class despite its heavier armament. The partially assembled kit distribution model introduced variable build quality into early Buzzard production, with hastily assembled vehicles exhibiting reliability issues that factory-finished examples did not share. Commanders typically pair Buzzards with faster Falcons and Hawks to screen their reduced escape speed while the Buzzard's weapons engage targets at range.
text.deployment: The Buzzard serves as the fire support element in mixed formations alongside Falcons and Hawks, using its heavier armament to engage threats at distances the faster but lighter-armed companions cannot reach. Militia commanders position it in concealed or elevated firing locations where its reduced speed poses less risk of surprise contact, relying on Falcon and Hawk partners to screen approaches. Peripheral forces favor it as an affordable alternative to fusion-powered fire support vehicles for planetary defense and anti-raider operations where budget constraints rule out BattleMech-class assets.
text.battleHistory:
Quikscell Company introduced the Buzzard in 3076, near the conclusion of the Jihad, targeting markets on worlds stripped of combat vehicle inventories during years of fighting. The Richvale facility designed the Buzzard to complement rather than replace the Falcon, providing a standoff fire platform affordable to the same militia clients that had kept the Falcon in production for over fifty years. Distribution proceeded through the partially assembled kit network that had defined Quikscell's commercial approach across all their products. Some clients fielded Buzzards before final assembly was complete, suffering mechanical failures during combat that undermined the vehicles' early operational reputation.

In 3148, the Moriguchi Militia deployed Buzzards alongside Falcons against Rim Territories slavers operating south of Settsu on Galedon V. The Buzzards provided the longer-range fire support that the faster but lighter-armed Falcons could not deliver, engaging bandit BattleMechs at distances that prevented the raiders from closing to their preferred fighting range. The combined formation proved effective, with the slavers unable to bring their larger units to bear before concentrated hovercraft fire degraded their combat effectiveness.

The Buzzard achieved more modest commercial success compared to the Falcon, with militia commanders generally preferring the faster original when both were available. The design nonetheless filled a real tactical niche as a dedicated standoff fire vehicle priced within reach of forces unable to afford fusion-powered alternatives. Through the ilClan period, the Buzzard remained available through Quikscell's distribution network as the long-range complement in mixed hovercraft formations.

text.deployment: The base Carnivore entered service with Clan Wolf in mid-3082, assigned initially to shore up frontline formations temporarily lacking sufficient BattleMech assets. Commanders integrate one or two into combined-arms formations where the twin Gauss rifles provide fire support at ranges that complement faster BattleMechs. The design has made its way to the open market in limited quantities, though the base version commands higher procurement costs than the Second Line variant, limiting its appeal to better-funded buyers. The Carnivore's presence in Hell's Horses combined-arms formations has grown since the transition of Weingarten to Horses control.

The HAG variant was developed to satisfy a Clan Jade Falcon procurement requirement, leveraging the Falcons' larger heavy weapons industrial base. The twin Gauss rifles give way to a hyper-assault Gauss cannon while the extended-range lasers are upgraded to pulse versions for improved accuracy at short and medium ranges. Machine gun bays are replaced with AP Gauss rifles for anti-infantry work, and a pair of anti-missile systems fitted to the turret provides additional protection against missile fire. Commanders operating mixed Carnivore formations recommend including at least one or two HAG models, as the area-damage profile of the HAG complements the precision striking power of the Gauss-armed base variant. Though designed originally as a trade vehicle for the Falcons, the HAG sees use within Wolf and Horses inventories as well.

The Second Line variant strips the Carnivore to a lower-cost configuration intended for broader commercial distribution. The extralight engine is replaced by a standard fusion plant, reducing performance, and the twin Gauss rifles are replaced by a single LB-X Class 10 autocannon capable of firing both solid and cluster rounds. The heavy machine guns are downgraded to light versions and the extended-range lasers are replaced with pulse models. Despite the reduced capability, the Second Line finds buyers among second-tier customers, with the Lyran Commonwealth and Wolves-in-Exile representing the primary purchasers. Critics note little meaningful difference between the two successor-state clients these days, though both continue to procure the variant in modest numbers through the open market.

production.manufacturer: Michaelson Heavy Industries|Kallon Weapon Industries|Yan Manufacturing

text.deployment: The standard Cavalry entered service with AFFC rapid-strike units in 3054, assigned primarily to hunter-killer teams tasked with suppressing enemy armor. Its combination of speed and missile firepower suited it for strikes from concealed positions, particularly in broken terrain and urban approaches where rotor craft could engage with limited exposure. The design saw early service across Draconis March and Sarna March noble guard formations and spread rapidly into the Chaos March mercenary market. Later Dark Age licensed production by Kallon Weapon Industries and Yan Manufacturing extended availability to Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine operators respectively.

Replacing the internal combustion engine with a fusion powerplant, the infantry variant trades missile armament for three medium lasers, machine guns, and a troop bay sized for a full foot platoon. Introduced in 3063 to address demand for a combined-arms delivery platform with organic fire support, this configuration filled a role distinct from the standard tank-buster. It found wide service in rapid-deployment formations requiring a helicopter capable of delivering infantry and then suppressing enemy positions. Kallon Weapon Industries began producing this variant during the early Republic era, initially under Duchy of Graham-Marik oversight before transitioning to Marik-Stewart Commonwealth and eventually Free Worlds League control.

The Infiltrator entered full production in 3085 following years of protracted development at Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion, incorporating vehicular stealth armor, a VTOL jet booster system, and chin-mounted Magshot Gauss rifles for a covert battle armor insertion role. Cal-Boeing could not meet demand from the start, and the Davion Department of Military Intelligence's Rabid Foxes received priority allocation from initial production runs. Most Infiltrators have since been assigned to units configured around Light Combat Team doctrine, where the helicopter fulfills transport, fire support, and covert insertion roles simultaneously. Cal-Boeing has not accepted orders from outside the Federated Suns, and the company has been exploring licensing arrangements to address ongoing financial pressures at Michaelson Heavy Industries.

The LRM variant provides extended-range fire support by substituting long-range missiles for the base configuration's short-range battery, allowing it to engage targets beyond the standard model's effective strike envelope. This makes the LRM variant better suited to open terrain operations and fire support roles where close-range strike tactics are less viable. Production began at Ruchbah in 3055 and continued through multiple ownership changes at that facility. Kallon Weapon Industries later added production capacity on Loyalty, extending availability to Free Worlds League and allied operators during the Dark Age.

Sacrificing one ton of armor protection to mount an additional SRM-2 launcher, this variant increases missile output at the cost of battlefield durability. The trade-off proved problematic in extended engagements, and elevated casualty rates were noted among units operating this configuration in the Chaos March, where reduced armor protection left crews more exposed during the close-range strikes for which the Cavalry was designed. Production remained concentrated at Michaelson's Ruchbah facility throughout its service life.

The TAG variant mounts a Target Acquisition Gear system, allowing the Cavalry to designate targets for artillery and homing munitions while retaining the speed and agility to avoid retaliation. Introduced in 3059, this configuration served primarily in forward observation and precision fire support roles, working alongside artillery assets to deliver indirect fire with greater accuracy than conventional spotting. Production at Ruchbah began under Federated Commonwealth control and the variant remained in service under subsequent facility owners. Kallon Weapon Industries added production capacity on Loyalty during the Dark Age, extending availability to Free Worlds League and allied operators.

production.targeting: Scuti Dualtar with Beagle Active Probe

text.deployment: The Centipede serves as the standard reconnaissance vehicle of the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces, deployed across nearly every LAAF front-line combined-arms formation and most planetary militia units. Its primary roles are advance scouting, screening operations, and flank security, with the integrated sensor suite giving reconnaissance lances a notable intelligence advantage over forces lacking comparable detection equipment. Distribution spans the breadth of Lyran space, though the design has grown scarcer since the loss of both primary manufacturing facilities during the Jade Falcon Incursion and Jihad.

production.targeting: Scuti Dualtar (Beagle Active Probe removed per TRO)

text.deployment: The SRM-armed Centipede is a field modification developed by Lyran troops and mercenary crews seeking a light fire-support platform rather than a dedicated scout. Stripping the vehicle's laser armament and sensor suite in favor of short-range missile racks transforms the Centipede into a light attack vehicle at the cost of its intelligence-gathering capability. Some mercenary crews further stripped the Beagle Active Probe for resale on the open market, fitting less capable replacement equipment. The modification is found almost exclusively in LAAF field units and mercenary formations operating in the Lyran periphery.
